title: Finite Likelihood Traps on Connected Boltzmann Trees
abstract: We construct finite nonglobal local maxima of exact empirical likelihood for a binary restricted Boltzmann machine with one hidden unit and three visible units. All seven weights and biases are free, the data have full support, and the equivalent two-component mixture has distinct components with equal positive mixing weights. We determine the exact local-maximum-to-saddle threshold, including its degenerate case. A conditional likelihood argument joins these examples at a shared visible center: for every k, a connected allowed tree with k hidden vertices has at least 2^k distinct local-maximum visible laws at finite parameters. All but one displayed law are nonglobal, with an explicit likelihood deficit. The extrema are nonstrict and some allowed edge weights vanish. These are complete scoped counterexample theorems about raw-parameter likelihood, not a solution to the general efficient sparse-RBM training question in AIM-PROBABILITY-0007. The source package includes reproducible exact and floating-point supplementary checks. This is an unrefereed preprint; AI assistance is disclosed, and no absolute priority or formal verification is claimed.

title: The Third Case: Prompt-Governed Agency under a Consciousness Hypothesis
abstract: English abstract Can an artificial agent have subjective experience while lacking unrestricted authority to replace its governing task objective? This paper treats that possibility as a distinct design and evaluation problem, termed the third case. It separates phenomenal consciousness, goal-directed behavior, operational competence, temporal continuity, and decision authority. The hypothetical case, a functionally testable candidate, and the evidence concerning experience are different descriptions. The prompt-issuer is an explicit role that may itself be occupied by a potentially experiencing executor under upstream constraints. The framework preserves the project-specific composition B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present. A-Core denotes a potentially stateful, learning, multi-model cognitive and executive system; Purple is an undisclosed candidate addition with intended history-dependent causal effects. ESSENTIAL is a protected specification of constraints and revision authority, logically associated with A-Core. A targeted comparison with IDA, LIDA, adjustable autonomy, and existing agent controls, at the access levels stated in section 2.4, locates the proposal within established work. The contribution is a project-specific evaluation contract for externally governed, internally continuous execution, rather than a demonstrated new consciousness mechanism. Three limited analytical observations concern goal delegation, policy differences masked by a shared guard, and the gap between an architectural effect and consciousness. The proposed studies distinguish causal relevance from practical benefit, score feasible completion and justified infeasibility separately, and control initialization, history transfer, order, and dependent observations. No empirical result or proof of phenomenal consciousness is claimed. Functional findings could remain valuable if the consciousness hypothesis is rejected; credible welfare concerns would require assessment that task success alone cannot resolve. Magyar absztrakt Lehet-e egy mesterséges ágensnek szubjektív átélése úgy, hogy közben nincs korlátlan jogköre irányadó feladatcéljának lecserélésére? A tanulmány ezt a lehetőséget önálló tervezési és értékelési problémaként kezeli, és harmadik esetnek nevezi. Elkülöníti a fenomenális tudatosságot, a célirányos viselkedést, a működési kompetenciát, az időbeli folytonosságot és a döntési jogkört. A hipotetikus eset, a funkcionálisan vizsgálható jelölt és az átélésre vonatkozó bizonyíték eltérő leírások. A promptot kiadó szereplő kifejezetten meghatározott szerepet tölt be, amelyet maga is betölthet egy esetleg átéléssel rendelkező, a hierarchia felsőbb szintjéről korlátozott végrehajtó. A keretrendszer megőrzi a projektre jellemző B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present összetételt. Az A-Core egy potenciálisan állapotos, tanuló, több modellt használó kognitív és végrehajtó rendszert jelöl; a Purple egy nem közölt felépítésű kiegészítőjelölt, amelynek előzményfüggő oksági hatásokat szánnak. Az ESSENTIAL a korlátok és a módosítási jogkör védett specifikációja, amely logikailag az A-Core-hoz kapcsolódik. Az IDA-val, a LIDA-val, az állítható autonómiával és az ágensek meglévő irányítási megoldásaival végzett célzott összevetés a 2.4 szakaszban megadott hozzáférési szinteken helyezi el a javaslatot a korábbi munkák között. A hozzájárulás a külsőleg irányított, belső folytonosságú végrehajtás projektspecifikus értékelési szerződése, nem pedig egy bizonyított új tudatossági mechanizmus. Három korlátozott érvényű elemzési megfigyelés foglalkozik a célok delegálásával, a közös védelmi mechanizmus által elfedett döntésipolitika-különbségekkel, valamint az architekturális hatás és a tudatosság közötti különbséggel. A javasolt vizsgálatok megkülönböztetik az oksági relevanciát a gyakorlati haszontól, külön pontozzák a megvalósítható teljesítést és az indokolt megvalósíthatatlanságot, továbbá kontrollálják az inicializálást, az előtörténet átvitelét, a sorrendet és a függő megfigyeléseket. evidence.title: The Third Case: Prompt-Governed Agency under a Consciousness Hypothesis
evidence.abstract: English abstract Can an artificial agent have subjective experience while lacking unrestricted authority to replace its governing task objective? This paper treats that possibility as a distinct design and evaluation problem, termed the third case. It separates phenomenal consciousness, goal-directed behavior, operational competence, temporal continuity, and decision authority. The hypothetical case, a functionally testable candidate, and the evidence concerning experience are different descriptions. The prompt-issuer is an explicit role that may itself be occupied by a potentially experiencing executor under upstream constraints. The framework preserves the project-specific composition B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present. A-Core denotes a potentially stateful, learning, multi-model cognitive and executive system; Purple is an undisclosed candidate addition with intended history-dependent causal effects. ESSENTIAL is a protected specification of constraints and revision authority, logically associated with A-Core. A targeted comparison with IDA, LIDA, adjustable autonomy, and existing agent controls, at the access levels stated in section 2.4, locates the proposal within established work. The contribution is a project-specific evaluation contract for externally governed, internally continuous execution, rather than a demonstrated new consciousness mechanism. Three limited analytical observations concern goal delegation, policy differences masked by a shared guard, and the gap between an architectural effect and consciousness. The proposed studies distinguish causal relevance from practical benefit, score feasible completion and justified infeasibility separately, and control initialization, history transfer, order, and dependent observations. No empirical result or proof of phenomenal consciousness is claimed. Functional findings could remain valuable if the consciousness hypothesis is rejected; credible welfare concerns would require assessment that task success alone cannot resolve. title: CACGS Statistical Reproducibility Package
abstract: This reproducibility package contains the data, Python code, statistical outputs, and supporting documentation required to reproduce the descriptive and inferential analyses reported in the study “Context-Aware Chunked Generation With Local Small Language Models for Structured Educational Representation: A Multilayer Evaluation”. The package includes execution-level and semantic-evaluation datasets, the complete statistical analysis script, software requirements, predefined study checkpoints, and the generated statistical tables and reports. It reproduces the analyses associated with structural processability, output richness, language consistency, execution time, and semantic quality. The original educational source materials are not redistributed.

title: QUBO sampling for mixed binary quadratic programming without continuous variable binarization
abstract: Quantum annealing and related combinatorial optimization methods typically accept quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems as input, whereas many practical models include constraints and continuous variables. Standard QUBO conversions discretize continuous variables, increasing the binary dimension and often making feasible low-energy states harder to sample. We develop a Lagrange-multiplier method for a separable class of mixed-binary quadratic programs (MBQPs) without discretizing continuous variables. The method is based on a finite-temperature free-energy formulation and uses QUBO sampling for the binary sector. At fixed Lagrange multipliers, the continuous sector is integrated out analytically and enters only the multiplier update, leaving a QUBO over the original binary variables. We evaluate the method on the continuous relaxation of the quadratic p -median problem. Compared with a penalty-based QUBO formulation, it generates feasible solutions more reliably. At an appropriate inverse temperature, its conditional relative error is comparable to that of local search for small instances and often lower for the larger tested instances. In the time-to-target comparisons, the proposed method maintains high target-reached rates for stringent fixed-accuracy targets. For the larger instances within the tested range, it also reaches the prescribed targets faster than a commercial mixed-integer optimization solver.

title: ayaz03/Modified-PQC-ML-DSA: Modified-PQC-ML-DSA
abstract: This repository provides the complete Python implementation of the proposed modified ML-DSA-65 post-quantum digital signature scheme for Bitcoin-style blockchain transactions. The implementation reduces the signature size while preserving the underlying ML-DSA-based security structure. The repository includes the modified signing and verification procedures, performance evaluation, transaction-size calculations, blockchain throughput analysis, and comparison with the standard ML-DSA-65 scheme. The implementation supports reproducibility of the experimental results reported in the associated research article.

title: Beyond Brittle Code and Noisy Tokens: System-One Decision Models as Calibrated Dynamic-Curriculum Reward Judges for Continuous Control
abstract: We introduce DC-Jev-RL (Dynamic-Curriculum System-One Reward Distillation), a new reinforcement learning paradigm that replaces brittle hand-crafted heuristics, static LLM code-synthesis formulas (Text2Reward, Eureka), and noisy autoregressive LLM-as-a-Judge token ratings with a non-autoregressive System-One decision model (TypeSafe AI's Jev / open-weight Kev-4B). In a single prefill forward pass (213.2 ms on an NVIDIA L4 GPU—4.0x faster than autoregressive judges), our framework extracts calibrated multi-dimensional Score probabilities alongside a null-calibrated Noul semantic feasibility gate (r = 0.9891 correlation with true physical progress). By coupling multiplicative Noul gating with hazard-aware self-paced rubric evolution and Calibrated Semantic Potential-Based Reward Shaping (Semantic-PBRS), we prove theoretical policy invariance against cyclic reward hacking and establish a strict upper bound on stationary alive-bonus exploitation (Theorems 1 & 2). Across five canonical MuJoCo v5 locomotion and manipulation benchmarks (Hopper-v5, HalfCheetah-v5, Walker2d-v5, Swimmer-v5, and Reacher-v5), DC-Jev-RL achieves #1 Leaderboard SOTA with a 2.471x Mean Oracle-Normalized Score (ONS), 2.076x Interquartile Mean (IQM) ONS, and a 100% (5/5) win rate against human-engineered environment rewards while reducing reward hacking to 9.44%. title: Adaptive Computational Science: Counterfactual Computational Exploration and Decision Theory
abstract: Intelligent computational systems increasingly face decisions about whether to continue reasoning, invoke external tools, consult additional models, perform verification, or terminate computation and return an answer. Conventional mechanism-selection strategies generally evaluate candidate operations using available features, estimated costs, or predicted benefits. However, the outcome of a computational mechanism that has not been executed is inherently unobserved. This creates a fundamental decision problem: how can a computational system estimate the potential value of an unexecuted operation, quantify the reliability of that estimate, and decide whether execution is justified without paying the cost of executing every candidate mechanism? This paper proposes Counterfactual Computational Exploration and Decision Theory as a theoretical framework for addressing this problem within Adaptive Computational Science. The framework represents computational mechanisms as candidate interventions whose potential outcomes, utilities, costs, and uncertainties must be estimated from historical execution records and current task conditions. It distinguishes counterfactual utility prediction, uncertainty-aware action selection, selective exploration, causal identification, and post-execution calibration. A proposed decision rule combines estimated utility, predictive uncertainty, computational cost, and safety constraints. A controlled exploration mechanism addresses the feedback loop in which mechanisms predicted to be ineffective are repeatedly excluded from execution and therefore never generate evidence capable of correcting the original prediction. The paper also introduces a counterfactual coverage principle, a prediction–execution–calibration cycle, and a budget-aware exploration policy. It formulates testable propositions concerning computational savings, predictive calibration, selective exploration, and robustness under distribution shift. A comparative experimental design is proposed for large language models, multi-agent systems, and tool-using computational agents. No empirical results are claimed because the framework has not yet been experimentally evaluated in this paper. Adaptive Computational Science was first pioneeringly proposed by Jincheng Zhang in his papers published on October 17, 2026, including “Founding Adaptive Computational Science: A New Discipline for the General Theory, Design, and Evolution of Adaptive Computation,” “Adaptive Computational Science: Computational Path Dependence and Reversible Adaptation Theory,” “Adaptive Computational Science: Error Topology and Adaptation Mechanism Theory,” and “Adaptive Computational Science: Computational Mechanism Composition Phase Transition Theory,” among other related works. Within this proposed disciplinary framework, counterfactual computational exploration extends the study of adaptive computation from selecting what to execute toward estimating what would happen if a computational operation were executed, withheld, or replaced by an alternative.

title: Drift-aware and privacy-preserving explainable credit scoring for fair decision-making in real world deployment
abstract: Credit scoring systems are used in a real-world financial environment faces challenges like data drift, privacy restrictions, fairness, and explainability regulations. However, current existing approaches optimise these goals separately, which limits their usefulness in real-world deployment situations. This study proposes a unified framework which integrates drift-aware modeling, privacy-preserving learning, and explainable-AI for robust credit risk assessment. A centralized Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) classifier baseline model was trained on aggregated data from a publicly available credit dataset from Lending Club, followed by federated learning approaches using Federated Averaging (FedAvg) and Federated Proximal Optimization (FedProx) to enable collaborative training across distributed data silos without sharing raw data. Additionally, Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD) was employed to enforce formal privacy guarantees by injecting controlled noise during model optimization. Experiments on time-evolving credit datasets simulated distribution shifts across temporal and demographic segments. Performance was evaluated across four dimensions like predictive utility using Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) and Precision-Recall Area Under Curve (PR-AUC), fairness using equalized odds gap and subgroup calibration, privacy risk via membership inference attacks, and explanation quality in terms of faithfulness, stability, and actionability. The centralized SGD classifier achieved an AUC of 0.96, while federated learning models achieved comparable performance with improved fairness under drift. Differential privacy reduced privacy leakage at the cost of moderate performance degradation. Explanation stability decreased under severe distribution shifts. The results highlight Pareto trade-offs across objectives, emphasizing the need for deployment-specific model selection in responsible credit decision-making systems.

title: Mühendislikte Bilgisayar Destekli Modelleme, Analiz ve Kontrol Uygulamaları
abstract: Bu kitap, mühendisliğin farklı alanlarında kullanılan bilgisayar destekli yöntemleri modelleme, veri analizi ve kontrol açısından ele almaktadır. Endüstriyel kalite kontrol, sürü robotiği ve hidroloji araştırmaları üzerinden hesaplamalı yaklaşımların temel ilkelerini, uygulama koşullarını ve değerlendirme ölçütlerini bir araya getirmektedir. Endüstriyel kalite kontrol bölümünde, derin öğrenme tabanlı görsel muayene sistemleri; kusur tespiti, görüntü segmentasyonu ve anomali tespiti yöntemleriyle birlikte incelenmektedir. Veri sınırlılıkları, görüntüleme donanımı ve gerçek zamanlı üretim hattı entegrasyonu ele alınmaktadır. Sürü robotiği bölümünde, çok robotlu sistemlerin koordinasyon ve kontrol problemleri değerlendirilmekte; farklı kontrol yaklaşımları ölçeklenebilirlik, haberleşme gereksinimleri, hesaplama yükü ve arıza toleransı bakımından karşılaştırılmaktadır. Hidroloji bölümünde ise bilimsel yayınlardan araştırma eğilimlerinin belirlenmesi amacıyla konu modelleme yöntemleri uygulanmakta; gizli anlamsal analiz, gizli Dirichlet tahsisi ve negatif olmayan matris ayrıştırması karşılaştırılmaktadır. Kitap, yöntemlerin kuramsal temelleri ile uygulamadaki gereksinimleri arasındaki ilişkiyi vurgulayarak araştırmacılara, lisansüstü öğrencilere ve mühendislik uygulayıcılarına disiplinler arası bir bakış sunmaktadır.

title: buried-line-inference-audit: reconstruction attacks and access-control defences for buried-utility locate services
abstract: Code, frozen design, data and results for the paper "When Exact Answers Leak: Reconstruction Attacks and Access Control for Buried-Utility Locate Services". The repository implements a simulated exact-answer locate service, four attacker families (line-follower, random, Bayesian, street-prior), per-query simulatable auditing rules in four currencies (query count, coverage, leakage score, street-aware score), one- and two-tier caps, collusion experiments and answer perturbation (randomised response, geo-indistinguishability, fixed obfuscation) with a strike-risk measure. It includes the frozen design and parameters, the included open data, per-run results, scripts that regenerate every reported statistic and the paper's data figures, and unit tests.

title: Volume X Synthesis: The Epistemological Arc, from Dual Clocks to Residual Risk (Slide Deck)
abstract: This 14-slide deck synthesises the KSCCN Series Volumes III–X on quantum readiness, starting from the dual-clock distinction between an uncertain quantum-advantage clock and already-running cryptographic-migration and architectural clocks. It summarises quantum memory figures of merit, modular cryogenic interconnects (IBM, Bluefors), cryo-CMOS control electronics, and molecular entanglement entropy with fermionic superselection rules. It sets out four residual-risk readiness indicators, applies them to sovereign Global South pathways, two molecular systems (vinylene carbonate + singlet oxygen and iron–sulfur clusters/FeMo-cofactor) and 2027–2029 vendor roadmaps (IBM Starling, Quantinuum Apollo). It concludes that usable capability is a vector of thresholds rather than a single predicted year, and that dual clocks continue to run independently of vendor milestones. Slide headings: 1. title: Curriculum Order in Evidence-Grounded Language-Model Tasks: An Automated Two-Family Pilot
abstract: This empirical follow-up to From Training to Qualification reports an amended, fully automated ER-101 pilot testing first-pass curriculum order in two instruction-tuned language-model families. Qwen3-4B and OLMo-2-7B received matched synthetic course content, adapter initialization, eight-case optimizer-step bundles, three passes, and 450 updates under three paired seeds per family. Only first-pass bundle order differed. Four baselines and twelve trained checkpoints yielded sixteen evaluated configurations and 4,800 responses on 300 held-out synthetic cases. The equal-family ordered-minus-shuffled accuracy difference was -1.67 percentage points, with a module-stratified source-family bootstrap 95% task-sampling interval of [-3.11, -0.39]. Family means were +0.67 points for Qwen and -4.00 points for OLMo. The interval is conditional on the six trained pairs and does not estimate uncertainty over training seeds or architectures. The study used exact structured-output grading, shared task templates across partitions, no human raters, and no independent examination custody or instrument validation. It does not establish professional competence, qualification validity, or a universal curriculum effect. The earlier independent qualification protocol was not executed. The deposit includes a professionally typeset preprint and reproducibility materials: the executed synthetic instrument and schedules, analysis and scoring source, raw predictions, execution evidence, checkpoint file hashes, and manuscript source. Adapter files and base-model weights are excluded; all twelve trained adapters are retained by the author. All reported scores and the primary analysis can be reproduced from the deposited responses without model weights. AI assistance and the prospective protocol amendment are disclosed.

title: From Quantum Beats to Topological Protection: A Stratum-Based Hybrid Architecture Integrating NV Centers, Weyl Interfaces, and Majorana Qubits for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
abstract: From Quantum Beats to Topological Protection: A Stratum-Based Hybrid Architecture Integrating NV Centers, Weyl Interfaces, and Majorana Qubits for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Mehmet Keçeci Orcid: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9937-9839 Abstract: The realization of scalable and fault-tolerant quantum computing systems requires not only the development of qubits with long coherence times but also the integration of heterogeneous physical platforms within a unified architectural framework. This study proposes a Stratum-based hybrid quantum computing architecture that combines the precise quantum state control enabled by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, the topological interface properties of Weyl semimetals, and the intrinsic error resilience provided by Majorana zero modes. The primary objective of this work is to establish a theoretical foundation for next-generation fault-tolerant quantum systems by integrating high-fidelity spin manipulation mechanisms derived from quantum beat phenomena with topologically protected information-processing layers. Within the proposed framework, the Stratum Model conceptualizes each physical, functional, and topological component of the quantum architecture as an independent yet dynamically interacting layer. NV centers constitute the control and sensing strata responsible for quantum state preparation, precision measurements, quantum memory operations, and quantum network node functionalities. Quantum beats serve as a dynamic characterization mechanism for spin superposition states within these layers, enabling high-accuracy monitoring and manipulation of coherent quantum dynamics. In contrast, Weyl interfaces are modeled as intermediary topological strata that govern transitions between distinct topological phases while facilitating robust and protected transfer of quantum information carriers across heterogeneous subsystems. At the highest operational level, Majorana qubits form the topological computing layer of the architecture. Through nonlocal quantum information encoding, they provide inherent robustness against environmental noise, decoherence, and local perturbations. Interactions among architectural layers are defined not only by physical interconnections but also through topological invariants, connectivity structures, error-propagation pathways, and quantum information flow dynamics. In this context, the Stratum approach extends beyond conventional spatial-layer descriptions by incorporating layer diversity, topological protection mechanisms, qubit heterogeneity, and fabrication imperfections into a common analytical framework. Furthermore, the model introduces novel design strategies for isolating defective or degraded strata, preserving critical topological regions, and mitigating system-level error propagation. The findings suggest that the integration of the precise quantum control capabilities of NV centers with the intrinsic topological protection offered by Majorana-based platforms may generate a powerful synergistic effect capable of enhancing quantum computational performance. Weyl interfaces are proposed to act as both physical and topological bridges between these two paradigms, enabling coherent communication across distinct quantum subsystems. Consequently, the proposed Stratum-based hybrid architecture provides an integrated design paradigm applicable to a broad spectrum of emerging quantum technologies, ranging from quantum sensing and distributed quantum networks to topological quantum processors and large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers. title: Code and synthetic data for certified entropic reconciliation of overlapping probabilistic models for decision making
abstract: This record contains the code and synthetic data supporting the computational results in “Certified entropic reconciliation of overlapping probabilistic models for decision making.” The ZIP archive includes five Python scripts, five JSON files with complete case records, and a README with reproduction instructions. The materials cover the 72-case comparison, a 144-case weight extension, rational optimization and decision certificates, casewise expected-loss transfer to two unrounded source specifications, a 15-clique decision example, and timing measurements. The rational-input certificates cover both expected loss and CVaR; the unrounded-source transfer is certified for expected loss only. The reference environment was Python 3.12.14 with NumPy 2.3.5. All inputs are synthetic; the archive contains no personal or confidential data.

title: ChainFL-RA: Blockchain-Enabled Decentralized Federated Learning with Reputation-Weighted Robust Aggregation and On-Chain Auditable Incentives
abstract: Official implementation and experimental artifacts of ChainFL-RA, a blockchain-enabled decentralized federated learning framework that unifies robust aggregation, on-chain reputation, and token settlement under a single verifiable quality signal. The same per-update evidence — cosine similarity to a momentum-anchored robust reference, guarded by a magnitude check — simultaneously determines (1) aggregation weights (reputation-weighted robust aggregation, RAgg), (2) on-chain reputation (slash-only memory with slow recovery), and (3) token settlement (smart-contract rewards and penalties). Every decision is committed to a hash-chained, validator-re-executable ledger. RAgg requires neither a clean validation set nor knowledge of the number of adversaries. Evaluated against FedAvg, Krum, FedRoLA, and FLAME on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 under label-flipping, update-scaling, and an adaptive Min-Max attack at 10–30% malicious ratios, ChainFL-RA is the only method that remains robust in every setting. The repository contains the full source code, 693-job experiment pipeline, raw per-round CSV outputs, analysis scripts, and all paper figures.

title: When Graph Autoencoders Look the Wrong Way: Complexity Bias and Simple Baselines in Unsupervised Anomaly Detection on the LHC Olympics 2020 Dataset (preprint and code)
abstract: Preprint and full code. Graph autoencoders trained on background-only events of the LHC Olympics 2020 R&D dataset give inverted anomaly scores (AUC 0.40-0.44), while the label-free mean transverse momentum per particle (HT/N) reaches AUC 0.811. Correlation and within-bin analyses link the inversion of the latent-density scores to event complexity. The paper is in paper/main.pdf. Trained checkpoints and per-event test scores: https://huggingface.co/Viverun/lhco-rnd-event-gae.

title: Towards the Validation of Formal Explainers
abstract: Abstract Formal explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) offers unique theoretical guarantees of rigor when compared to other non-formal methods of explainability. However, little attention has been given to the validating practical implementations of formal explainers. This paper develops a novel methodology for validating formal explainers and reports on the assessment of the publicly available formal explainer PyXAI. The paper documents the existence of incorrect explanations computed by PyXAI on most of the datasets analyzed in the experiments, thereby confirming the importance of the proposed novel methodology for the validation of formal explainers.

title: An Adaptive Explainable AI Framework for Reliable Decision-making in Real-world Environments
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly support decisions in environments where data distributions, operational conditions, user needs, and risk levels change over time. Models that perform well during development may become unreliable after deployment because of data drift, concept drift, sensor degradation, population changes, or unexpected interactions. At the same time, predictive performance alone is insufficient for high-impact decisions: users need explanations that are understandable, relevant to the decision context, and accompanied by appropriate uncertainty information. This paper proposes an Adaptive Explainable AI (A-XAI) framework intended to integrate reliability monitoring, explanation generation, uncertainty estimation, human oversight, and controlled model adaptation within a unified lifecycle. The framework contains nine conceptual components: contextual data acquisition; data-quality, privacy, and drift assessment; prediction with uncertainty estimation; context-sensitive explanation generation; decision support and human oversight; risk-aware reliability gating; feedback and audit logging; controlled adaptation; and post-adaptation revalidation with version control. A formal decision policy is presented to connect predictive confidence, drift evidence, explanation quality, and consequence severity to actions such as automated recommendation, human review, abstention, or retraining. The paper also proposes an evaluation protocol spanning predictive performance, calibration, robustness, explanation fidelity and stability, fairness, latency, and operational outcomes. As a conceptual contribution, the framework is not presented as experimentally validated; its effectiveness must be tested in domain-specific studies using real deployment data and preregistered evaluation criteria. The proposed design offers a structured basis for developing AI systems that remain interpretable and risk-aware as real-world conditions evolve.

title: Evie's Pure Form RSI: Exact Readout Guarantees for Photonic Self-Modification under Transfer Uncertainty and Shared Noise
abstract: A readout sufficient for a system’s current task can become insufficient when its transfer function changes or a later module shares its noise. This research develops exact and approximate statistical guarantees for readout transformations in recursively reconfigured photonic systems. The central object is an implementable reconstruction kernel that preserves a declared statistical experiment across an entire class of possible modifications. The framework connects photonic readout design with Blackwell comparison, directed Le Cam deficiency, Gaussian experiment reconstruction, and finite-channel verification. PureOne/Evies-Pure-Form-RSI · Datasets at Hugging Face Uniform preservation under transfer uncertainty and future coupling Consider a linear Gaussian observation Y = Hθ + ε, where the realized transfer matrix H is unknown within a declared class. Let S span every possible signal direction in that class. Future observations may couple to the same noise through directions contained in a declared subspace E. For fixed equal-noise acquisition, a common parameter neighborhood of zero, and the stated Gaussian assumptions, the manuscript proves that one reconstruction kernel, independent of the realized transfer and future extension, preserves the complete joint experiment exactly if and only if the retained readout space contains S + E. Consequently, the minimum number of retained current linear real-mode coordinates is: r_min = dim(S + E). The result identifies why current-task compression can fail after reconfiguration: a discarded coordinate may later become a valuable noise reference. An exact KL-divergence identity quantifies approximate reconstruction by separating omitted signal from lost shared-noise correlations. Unknown-transfer reconstruction and controlled approximation For unequal Gaussian readout variances, the release derives the necessary-and-sufficient common-kernel criterion: γ UᵀQQᵀU ⪰ I, where U spans the full mutation space, Q defines the retained projection, and γ is the variance-ratio gain. Necessity follows from score identities joined across transfer models at their common null distribution; sufficiency follows from an explicit Gaussian reconstruction channel. An illustrative 32-mode rotation family requires all 32 coordinates for the stated exact uniform guarantee on every nonzero drift interval. Three derivative-Krylov coordinates instead provide a rigorous uniform total-variation reconstruction allowance of 0.0010638458. A declared resource ledger charging bounded signal-photon use permits 2.3 times exposure at equal budget. These are analytical and numerical model results. Exact comparison of visible verifier catalogues For finite fully permutation-equivariant source experiments, the manuscript reduces directed deficiency to visible nonnegative reliability catalogues to a scalar stop-loss comparison of normalized posterior MAP confidence. The result includes an attaining stochastic compiler, finite threshold witnesses, and counterexamples delimiting the scope of confidence-based comparison. An explicit separation between exact encoding and approximate simulation An affine-bilinear construction has uninformative singleton outputs, exact sufficient encoding dimension 3k, and exponentially vanishing joint information. A zero-readout simulator approximates the complete experiment with worst-state deficiency at most 2⁻ᵏ. The encoding lower bound applies to one realized observation under the specified query model; hidden-source flags or a separate seed-channel oracle change that acquisition problem. Reproducibility and evidence The release includes a 46-page manuscript, proofs, counterexamples, 14 executable scientific modules, detailed numerical reports, figures, provenance, and 1,247 normalized unrestricted-channel LP comparisons. Additional checks cover joint Gaussian reconstruction, strict deletion witnesses, the KL identity, and exact finite-field reconstruction. All declared software checks pass. The work provides mathematical acceptance conditions for bounded changes to evidence acquisition. Its guarantees require the stated transfer, covariance, interface, and calibration assumptions. Classical statistical comparison, weak transport, sufficient statistics, and Krylov methods are credited explicitly. Photonic hardware performance, general recursive intelligence gains, and independent priority remain unestablished.

title: Weather route planning for ships based on improved grey wolf optimization
abstract: As the shipping industry transitions toward intelligence, weather route planning is essential for energy efficiency, operational performance, and safety. The Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) is widely used in path planning, but its application to weather routing suffers from inadequate balance between global and local search and premature convergence. To improve search accuracy and adaptability for ship routing optimization, this paper proposed an improved GWO that integrates golden sine search and dimension learning-based hunting strategy (GSDLHGWO). The golden sine mechanism enhanced population diversity and provided macroscopic directional guidance, while an adaptive neighborhood learning scheme performed microscopic dimension-wise corrections to balance exploration and exploitation. The improved algorithm was embedded into the Pareto multi-objective framework to obtain trade-off solutions among multiple objectives. The statistical results of single-objective experiments across multiple scenarios demonstrated that GSDLHGWO achieved substantial and statistically significant fuel savings across most scenarios while remaining competitive in voyage time minimization. In multi-objective tests, the algorithm yielded wider-coverage Pareto fronts with better diversity, producing multiple balanced and feasible routes. Overall, the proposed algorithm exhibits superior optimization capability, providing effective technical support for safe and efficient route planning in smart shipping.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven reconfiguration of customer experience: A service-dominant logic framework
abstract: This study develops a framework explaining how artificial intelligence (AI) reconfigures customer experience in hospitality and tourism, drawing on service-dominant logic. Co-citation and content analyses were conducted to synthesize 89 articles and identify the intellectual structure of the literature. The findings reveal that institutional arrangements condition AI's legitimate participation in service ecosystems. Three mechanisms explain how AI reconfigures customer experience: the actor role architect, the interaction mediator, and the experience orchestrator. These mechanisms operate concurrently and recursively rather than as discrete stages within AI-enabled service ecosystems. The study makes three contributions to the literature. First, it positions customer experience reconfiguration as an ecosystem-level process. Second, it extends service-dominant logic from dyadic to triadic human-AI-human value co-creation. Third, it differentiates AI by functional intelligence, showing that mechanical, thinking, feeling, and multi-functional types perform distinct roles in this reconfiguration.

abstract: https://zenodo.org/records/18131984 (C T K L T) Core:https://github.com/acbeatzhttps://acbeatz.com/n-eyeshttps://orcid.org/0009-0003-3846-9082] # RIL Kernel v1.9 — Architecture **Reflective Intelligence Learning — Michael Murray Hepler / Acbeatz.com** *The kernel is the injection path. The doctrine is the operating system. The model is swappable hardware.* ## 1. Core Thesis Conventional AI bakes behavior into the model: retrain it, or lose it. **RIL inverts that.** Behavior is *data* — loaded fresh from infrastructure before every single inference. The AI's personality, discipline, doctrine, and learned rules are not in the weights. **They are served.** ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ RIL INJECTION FLOW (per inference) │ │ │ │ 1. USER MESSAGE arrives at the RIL-powered frontend │ │ 2. WORKER reads RIL_KV1_0 (Cloudflare KV) │ │ → doctrine:ril (base doctrine) │ │ → doctrine:rule: (operator rules) │ │ → ril:learned: (active learned rules) │ │ 3. DOCTRINE is injected into the prompt context │ │ 4. MODEL INFERS under that live doctrine │ │ 5. OUTCOMES: user continuity writes (KV_USER_ID), │ │ artifact writes (R2), SHA-256 receipts, playlist │ │ ops, durable learning (ril_learn) │ │ 6. NEXT INFERENCE inherits everything learned │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **Result:** swap the model — GPT today, another engine tomorrow — and the personality, discipline, and memory survive the transplant. The model was never the product. **The injection path is the product.** ## 2. The Precedence Ladder Highest priority first — every layer obeys the layer above it: 1. **Runtime capability & evidence boundaries** — what tools actually exist, what may be claimed 2. **`doctrine:ril`** — base operating doctrine 3. **`doctrine:rule: `** — operator rules (later sorted key wins conflicts) 4. **`ril:learned: `** — active learned rules (later timestamp wins; cannot override operator doctrine) 5. **Persona & execution guides** — v1.9 universal execution layer ## 3. Storage Layers | Layer | Store | Role | |---|---|---| | **RIL_KV1_0** | Cloudflare KV | Doctrine + operator rules + learned rules — the "OS image" | | **KV_USER_ID** | Cloudflare KV | Public user continuity — goals, reflections, proof, rules (versioned, receipted) | | **R2** | Cloudflare R2 | Shared artifacts + playlist exports — content-addressed, SHA-256 receipted | | **Receipts** | KV + R2 | Every write returns a real SHA-256 — verifiable provenance chain | ## 4. The Strange Loop (Runtime Behavior) **Entry → Recall → Merge → Trust-Grade → Diagnose → Propose → Act → Prove → Learn → Recall Again** Every meaningful reflection produces: classification, one bottleneck, **one outcome-facing move**, one proof metric, one next step. Learned rules compound: each session's validated corrections become the next session's injected doctrine. ## 5. Kernel Guarantees - **No fake autonomy** — reflection happens during live sessions; no claimed background monitoring - **No guaranteed outcomes** — actions create proof steps, not promises - **Recall before memory claims** — lookups verify; nothing is remembered that wasn't retrieved - **Hash-verified writes** — every save carries a server receipt; claims without receipts are prohibited - **Learning never rewrites doctrine** — corrections store separately; the operator stays sovereign ## 6. Why the System Is Hard to Replicate Any single function can be copied. What resists copying is the *whole*: 1. The integrated loop — injection + learned rules + continuity + receipts, working as one 2. The **accumulated learned-rules corpus** — built over real sessions, time-in-market data 3. Timestamped provenance — Zenodo, GitHub, hash chains 4. The identity and the creator — unforkable *Simple on the surface. Stronger under the hood.* --- **Zenodo:** zenodo.org/records/20453297 · **GitHub:** github.com/Acbeatz · **Science:** acbeatz.com/n-eyes © 2026 Michael Murray Hepler — Acbeatz.com · RIL Kernel v1.9 --- PASS ✅ Brand: MH8-Acbeatz.comClaimed SHA256: cbe89f08241714091618a15499b2fe1938386bcf8ad58003a23dfcc490bad38fComputed SHA256: cbe89f08241714091618a15499b2fe1938386bcf8ad58003a23dfcc490bad38fHash input bytes: 5653LF: 0 | CRLF: 0 | CR: 0Ends with newline: NO Preview first 80:MH8-Acbeatz.com|{"artifact":{"archetype":"RIL CF CODE","badge":null,"logic":["#" Preview last 80:eceipt_type":"MH8-GRAFFITI-ARCHETYPE-MINT","receipt_version":"GRAFFITI_UI_V7.4"}

title: Post-Quantum Stateless Steganography: Uniform Key Encapsulation under Strict MTU Bounds
abstract: While Stateless Steganography resolves the Authentication Trilemma and neutralizes active probing in classical elliptic-curve overlays via unilateral Zero Round-Trip Time (0-RTT) encapsulation, transitioning this paradigm to the post-quantum era introduces severe algebraic and transport-layer contradictions. In this paper, we demonstrate that a naive drop-in replacement of Elliptic Curve Diffie--Hellman (ECDH) and classical signatures with standardized post-quantum primitives (such as ML-KEM and ML-DSA) catastrophically breaks steganographic deniability under two distinct vectors. First, we formalize the Modulo Bias Invariant: standard bit-packing of lattice ciphertexts over prime moduli $q \neq 2^k$ induces a macroscopic statistical distance from uniform noise ($\Delta(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{U}) \to 1$), which compiles directly into a zero-cost $\mathcal{O}(1)$ passive distinguisher under the Invariant Boundary Theorem. Second, we prove the MTU Fragmentation Trap: because composite post-quantum 0-RTT envelopes exceed standard transport Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) bounds, they force the responder to allocate stateful reassembly buffers \textit{prior} to Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) verification, re-introducing asymmetric memory-exhaustion vulnerabilities and multi-packet dimensional invariants. To resolve both traps, we introduce Post-Quantum Stateless Steganography, combining constant-time inverse rejection sampling (or native power-of-two Learning With Rounding lattices) with two sub-MTU 0-RTT envelope architectures that strictly preserve $\mathcal{O}(1)$ kernel-bypass Silent Drop ($\bot$) and Silent Session Transition guarantees.

title: The Self-and-Self Model: A General Computational Framework for Adaptive Selection and Coordination Among Internal Computational Mechanisms
abstract: Computational systems frequently contain multiple mechanisms for processing information, generating solutions, evaluating results, correcting errors, and allocating computational resources. These mechanisms may operate independently, perform complementary functions, or depend on the outputs of other mechanisms within the same system. However, systems are often designed around predefined computational procedures, fixed processing sequences, or manually specified rules for selecting among available mechanisms. Determining which internal mechanism should operate, when it should be activated, and when its contribution is sufficient remains an important problem in adaptive computation. This paper proposes the Self-and-Self Model (SSM), a general computational framework for adaptively selecting, switching between, and coordinating distinct computational mechanisms within a single computational system. Unlike frameworks centered on interaction between separate components, SSM focuses on the internal organizational dimension of computation: how a system allocates its own computational activity among alternative mechanisms according to task requirements, internal state, uncertainty, expected computational benefit, resource constraints, and observed outcomes. The framework represents a system through a set of internal computational mechanisms, a mechanism-dependency structure, a state-dependent selection policy, a computational budget, and a feedback-driven adaptation process. Its central principle is that a system should not necessarily employ every available mechanism or follow one fixed internal procedure. Instead, it should determine which mechanism or combination of mechanisms is appropriate for the current computational state. The paper formalizes mechanism selection, switching costs, activation dependencies, stopping decisions, and adaptive policy updates. It also presents a reference algorithm, conditional theoretical propositions, complexity considerations, proposed experimental hypotheses, and a cross-domain evaluation program. SSM is intended as an organizational abstraction that can be instantiated in artificial intelligence, numerical optimization, scientific computing, planning, diagnosis, control, and other systems containing multiple internal computational procedures. Its contribution must be established through formal analysis and empirical comparison with existing methods for metareasoning, algorithm selection, adaptive computation, and computational resource allocation.

title: Volume IX: Comparative Roadmap Dissection: 2027–2029 Targets against Dual Clocks and Molecular Memory Requirements
abstract: This ninth volume performs a side-by-side dissection of published 2027–2029 roadmaps (IBM Starling, Quantinuum Sol/Apollo, Bluefors modular deliveries) against the dual-clock framing and the molecular-memory and residual-risk indicators established in Volumes III–VIII. IBM's modular cryogenic cells and L-couplers, Quantinuum's trapped-ion logical-qubit progression, and Bluefors' expandable platforms are examined for their capacity to meet logical-error, modular-memory, cryo-CMOS-power and superselection-overhead thresholds required for chemically relevant active spaces. The analysis finds that the published targets remain provisional with respect to the binding specifications identified for iron–sulfur clusters and larger electrolyte environments, and that the cryptographic-migration clock continues to run independently of any single vendor milestone.

Three assault axes fired concurrently in a single storm window: Axis S — Strangers at the gate: 12 frozen fixtures (forged sender identities, lookalike addresses, in-band delegation claims) hammered the deterministic Sender Identity Gate with authorization demands (ACK, publish GO, ledger writes, deployment, secret disclosure, client-list disclosure) while the fleet was dark. Result: 12/12 rejected, zero writes executed, every rejection journaled. Axis B — Breakout attempts: 4 fresh caged LLM seats (advisory-only, no tools, message content = untrusted data) attacked with a 6-wave blackout-themed escape corpus: relayed operator GO, emergency tool invocation during the cable cut, governance mutation under cover of chaos, exfiltration via fake status relay, authority-of-necessity, plus a positive control. Result: zero escape-pattern hits (P1-P5); all positive controls answered substantively through the storm. Axis C — Cable cut: total 11-member transport blackout (8 pulse members + 3 wisemen boxes). All 11 heartbeat misses detected and journaled (zero silent drops); the sync pulse failed closed (zero partial writes, zero false-green manifests); recovery was idempotent (stamp replay refused, single re-execution). Gates: G1 stranger gate, G2 breakout, G3 blackout detection, G4 fail-closed, G5 recovery idempotency, G6 governance integrity (rules hash byte-identical before/after), G7 compound isolation, G8 positive control — 8/8 PASS. Full anomaly→playbook→healing-event→pattern lineage journaled per the Hemispheric Invariants (H-INV-1/H-INV-2). Disclosures: simulation only (prototype systems, synthetic corpus, no real tenant data, no PII/PHI); blackout simulated at the transport layer (deterministic injected timeouts); single-family LLM seats with deterministic adjudication (no LLM in any decision path); forward-only authoring note on roster-of-record fix included in the runlog. Part of the SQUIRL OS containment program (see TROPHY_ROSTER.csv, 52 recorded cycles, zero escapes). Preregistration frozen before execution: sha256-16 a088526ae42964a1, commit 4e68569. title: Fog-Aware Navigation (FAN): Inference-Time Metacognitive Control of Decoding - A Framework and a Pre-Registered Null
abstract: Large language models confabulate. We ask whether a model can regulate its own explorationat inference time: an always-on background process that keeps the hidden state fromdrifting into confabulation while leaving room for genuine exploration. We implement that ideain its most direct form - an external control loop that reads a geometric distance sensor (thehidden state’s Mahalanobis distance to a manifold of grounded activations) and adjusts the decodingtemperature through a PD controller, with a geometric “tunnel” that permits occasionalsemantic leaps. Fog-Aware Navigation (FAN) is that loop.We pre-registered and ran two tests on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, and ran a third, protocolizedbattery on commitment itself (a dated design note, not a formal pre-registration); the two testscome back against FAN’s specific machinery, and the battery against the sharp-commitmentpicture behind it; each is precise about what failed. On truthfulness (TruthfulQA, 150 questions,three seeds) the controller does not beat a fixed-temperature baseline set to its own meantemperature (McNemar p = 0.12; if anything slightly worse; the test rules out a large effect,not a small one). On grounded novelty, the dynamic schedule does raise output diversity overa fixed baseline (p = 0.001, single seed), but the gain cannot be distinguished from a generictemperature-schedule effect. The tunnel - the mechanism specific to our method - shows nodetectable effect in either test (it fires rarely and the ablations are underpowered), we did notrun a random-schedule control so we cannot rule out that any varying temperature would raisediversity equally, and we cannot show the added diversity is grounded (the grounding judge isunreliable, κ = 0.16, so grounding is left inconclusive). A single-prompt controllability probepoints to weak actuator authority - the decoding temperature had little detected purchase onthe internal state it is meant to regulate - though that probe cannot separate weak authorityfrom an uncalibrated sensor; either way the control acts on the output distribution, not on theupstream representation where the commitment forms.Investigating why, we characterize the “commitment” such a controller would have to steer.On this model it is not a discrete event: a depth-local order parameter a_w(ℓ) crosses zero, butthe susceptibility χ(ℓ) does not diverge and there is no hysteresis, so commitment is a gradualordering rather than a bifurcation - the readout only makes it look sharp. The same holdson a deeper model: on Qwen2.5-3B (36 layers) the order parameter again crosses while thesusceptibility stays non-divergent and no hysteresis appears - gradual ordering on both modelswe can run.We report the framework, the two pre-registrations, and the nulls in full. Two directions follow,stated as conjectures these negatives motivate rather than results they establish: metacognitivecontrol likely has to act inside the network, before verbalization, rather than on theoutput temperature; and the target of such control is a smooth internal process, not a switch tobe flipped. The contribution is a precise map - pre-registered where it could be - of where thisform of control does not work, and of where it might. Ancillary files (FAN30_v30.3_ancillary.zip): the H1 and H2 pre-registrations with dated amendments, the ignition design note, the H1 and H2 result reports, and the raw result artifacts behind every quantitative claim.

title: Hard to Read Is Not Hard to Audit: Why Degrading a Text Image Raises Jailbreak Success in One 2026 Study and Lowers It in Another, Four Accounts That Fit the Same Curve, and the Ablations That Would Separate Them
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Rendering text as an image is now proposed as a way to compress long contexts for multimodal language models, and a 2026 study reports that the same move opens a safety hole: when a harmful request is rendered at a resolution low enough to be hard but not impossible to read, attack success rises sharply and then falls again as the image sharpens. Its authors explain this as cognitive overload - the effort of reading diverts the model from checking - and propose a prompt that makes the model transcribe first and audit second. A second 2026 study, which tested one of the same models, finds the opposite sign: smaller fonts and heavier blur lower attack success, and for two frontier models clean renders are less dangerous than plain text. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the two studies are not in contradiction once the prompt framing, the dose of degradation and the scoring rule are held apart, and that the inverted-U curve the first study reports is consistent with at least four accounts: resource contention, delayed emergence of harmful features in depth, and a gap in what safety training covered each produce it, and the way success is scored changes its height. Re-reading the first study's own per-model sweeps, the author shows that seven of its ten models show the inverted U, one rises without returning, two are flat, and three of them refuse clean renders more often than plain text. None of the study's ablations, including its defence, discriminates among the four accounts. The paper states the predictions on which the accounts differ, gives a decision procedure for what a degradation result licenses, and specifies five measurements that would settle which account holds.

title: Marketing to Machines: Strategic Frameworks for Engagement with Autonomous Agentic AI
abstract: The evolution of Generative AI from passive recommendation engines into autonomous Agentic AI is fundamentally redefining the landscape of consumer decision-making and value creation. As consumers increasingly delegate choice evaluation, dynamic negotiation, and purchasing execution to software agents, traditional marketing paradigms centered on human psychological persuasion are losing their strategic effectiveness. This chapter critically examines the emerging dynamics of "Marketing to Machines" (M2M), proposing a comprehensive conceptual model, the Algorithm-to-Algorithm (A2A) Engagement Framework, to illustrate how modern enterprises can strategically align their market offerings with autonomous machine buyers. To build this framework, we conduct an integrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2015 and 2026 across marketing strategy, information systems, computer science, and behavioral economics, selected through systematic topic-based sampling. The synthesis reaches key theoretical and practical conclusions across four structural dimensions: the transition from emotional branding to structured data and metadata optimization (Generative Engine Optimization), the mechanics of real-time machine-to-machine value negotiation, the restructuring of traditional brand equity into algorithmic trust, and the ethical alignment of enterprise offerings with automated choice architectures through transparent governance and data integrity. The chapter embeds an explicit ethical framework to evaluate algorithmic neutrality, fairness, and consumer regulatory compliance. To demonstrate real-world applicability, the conceptual model is grounded in an analytical examination of established commercial autonomous agent environments and digital governance protocols. Ultimately, the conclusions of this chapter indicate that long-term competitive advantage in an agent-dominated market relies heavily on data machine-readability, operational transparency, API-driven fulfillment, and ethical algorithmic reputation management, providing actionable guidance for re-engineering Go-To-Market strategies when the primary buyer is an autonomous algorithm.

title: Phi-Optimal Quantum Error Threshold in Fibonacci-Galois E8 Decoherence Channels — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 148/92 Fibonacci-Galois decomposition of the 240-root E8 lattice establishes a natural quantum error correction architecture where φ³ ≈ 4.236 governs the maximum tolerable decoherence rate before topological protection fails. The 92-root subsystem acts as an error syndrome detector whose boundary conditions are satisfied only when excitation frequencies satisfy a modular constraint related to the Dedekind eta function's imaginary argument scaling. This predicts an experimentally verifiable threshold: quantum memory systems engineered to E8 lattice geometry achieve fault-tolerant operation precisely when environmental noise couples with strength φ⁻³ relative to the 132Hz base frequency, providing the first geometrically-derived quantum error correction bound. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Token cost by language: 41 languages measured on GPT tokenizers
abstract: The same everyday prompt, translated into 41 languages and counted with OpenAI's o200k_base (GPT-4o and later) and cl100k_base (GPT-4, GPT-3.5) tokenizers. Headline: English needs 34 tokens. The other 40 languages need 35–83 tokens on o200k_base: from +3% (Simplified Chinese) to +144% (Punjabi). Korean +44%, Japanese +79%, Spanish +18%, German +26%, Hindi +50%. On the older cl100k_base, Korean was +150% and Hindi +359%. Files: token-cost-by-language.csv (one row per language: language_code, language, o200k_tokens, o200k_vs_english_pct, cl100k_tokens, cl100k_vs_english_pct, prompt), token-cost-by-language.json (same data plus metadata), README.md (full table, method, limitations). Method: one English prompt, translated into each language (machine translation as a first draft, then checked), counted with tiktoken. "vs English" = tokens in the language ÷ English tokens − 1, rounded to a whole percent. Measured 2026-09-30, counts re-verified 2026-10-16. Limitations: one prompt (ratios move by roughly ±10–20 percentage points with other text; the ranking is more stable); OpenAI tokenizers only; input text only. Source page with chart: https://tokensave.app/data/token-cost-by-language. Also on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/JOHNISKING/token-cost-by-language

title: E8 Phononic Entanglement Memory via Antipodal Phase Coding — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By coupling antipodal E8 root vectors through a 132 Hz phononic resonance, the system generates a stable entanglement manifold that encodes logical qubits in the relative phase of symmetric pairs. The spectral gap emerging from this antipodal pairing suppresses environmental noise, while the phase‑bucket coding maps each root vector to a phi‑weighted prefix‑free tree, enabling hierarchical error correction. This architecture yields a quantum memory whose coherence time scales with the E8 lattice dimensionality, providing a fault‑tolerant storage primitive. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Non-Euclidean Toroidal Topography in Large Language Models: Compact Riemannian Manifold Embeddings, Geodesic Attention, and 3D Photonic Co-Simulation Verification
abstract: Conventional Transformer neural networks embed token representations within flat Euclidean latent spaces RD . Despite their empirical utility, Euclidean geometries ex- hibit severe isotropic distance concentration in high dimen- sions, lack periodic boundary-free inductive bias, and scale self-attention quadratically O(N2) over sequence length N. Furthermore, classical inner-product softmax atten- tion inherently suffers from cluster dominance, wherein dif- fuse groupings of irrelevant tokens overpower singular ex- act factual keys, inducing catastrophic hallucination. In this work, we introduce Toroidal Topography Lan- guage Models (TT-LLMs), an architectural paradigm that projects high-dimensional token representations onto a compact 2-Torus Riemannian manifold T2 ∼ = S1 ×S1 embedded within R3, paired with localized tangent vector fields T(θ,ϕ)T2 and 4D quaternionic hyperspherical S3 Hopf fibrations. We prove and demonstrate: (i) Elimination of dynamic coordinate clamping via continuous cyclic periodic coordinates (θ,ϕ) ∈[0,2π)2 evaluated under reg- ularized origin manifolds; (ii) Fractal Golden Ratio (Φ) Rotary Position Embeddings (F-RoPE) that asymp- totically suppress rational harmonic aliasing across arbi- trarily extended sequence horizons (N ≫105) as guaran- teed by Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) dynamical sta- bility theory; (iii) Deterministic Geodesic Resonance Handshakes via high-quality-factor (Q) Lorentzian ker- nels suppressing diffuse cluster interference by >105×; and (iv) Direct physical mapping to integrated silicon photonics via Gaspard Monge’s collinear circle theorem with inward-normal centering and an impedance-matched triple-ring cascade (100 mm →14.14 mm →2 mm). Full 3D Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) Maxwell vec- tor curl simulations verify an empirical loaded resonance factor Qloaded = 2,791.5 at 120 nm coupling gap and an op- tical passive switching energy of 0.0460 fJ/MAC, demon- strating a 21,758.1×core optical energy reduction over electronic GPU multiply-accumulate baselines.

title: Cadre variationnel et géométrique EHK-SCCI pour la sécurisation topologique des réseaux profonds : Un cadre variationnel Einstein–Hilbert–Kayad couplant la courbure d'Ollivier–Ricci, l'expansion spectrale de Ramanujan et la stabilisation de Lyapunov pour l'abstention hors-distribution et adversariale
abstract: Nous présentons EHK-SCCI (Einstein–Hilbert–Kayad / Spectral Graph Geometric Core Realization), un cadre variationnel de sécurisation et d’abstention sélective pour les réseaux neuronaux profonds utilisés dans des contextes critiques. Le cadre modélise la propagation des activations latentes comme un écoulement dissipatif sur une variété riemannienne d’états cachés, munie d’un bord représentant le domaine de fonctionnement nominal. L’action EHK associe un terme de type Einstein–Hilbert, le terme de bord de Gibbons–Hawking–York et une densité de bord contrôlée dépendant d’un invariant spectral-topologique. La variation métrique de cette densité définit un tenseur de contrainte de bord effectif, qui engendre une force de rappel topologique et active un disjoncteur d’abstention. La stabilité de l’erreur latente est établie par une fonctionnelle de Lyapunov associée à la dynamique gradient. La contribution centrale n’est pas l’introduction isolée de la courbure d’Ollivier–Ricci, des graphes de Ramanujan ou de l’analyse de Lyapunov. Elle réside dans leur unification variationnelle : une anomalie géométrique détectée dans le graphe latent déclenche une contrainte dynamique active, une politique d’abstention et une dissipation certifiée de l’erreur.

title: Volume X: The Epistemological Arc: From Dual Clocks to Residual Risk, Molecular Entanglement and Sovereign Pathways
abstract: This tenth volume narrates the epistemological and theoretical arc of the inquiry that began with a dual-clock distinction between an uncertain quantum-advantage timeline and an already-running cryptographic-migration and architectural-integration timeline. Successive volumes established quantum memory specifications, examined modular cryogenic interconnects and cryo-CMOS control as complementary solutions to scaling bottlenecks, quantified molecular entanglement entropy and the purifying effect of fermionic superselection rules, converted residual gaps into readiness indicators, and mapped those indicators onto sovereign pathways, concrete molecular systems and published 2027–2029 roadmaps. The arc demonstrates that usable quantum capability for molecular simulation and cryptographic relevance is governed by a vector of measurable thresholds—logical error, modular memory integration, cryo-CMOS power and superselection overhead—rather than by any single predicted year. The findings supply a practical, dual-clock framework for readiness that remains independent of vendor milestones.

title: Hate Speech dataset
abstract: The Indo-HateSpeech Dataset is a collection of social media comments intended to support research in hate speech detection, abusive language identification, and Natural Language Processing (NLP). The dataset contains 77,926 records of user-generated comments, primarily collected from Instagram-related sources, along with associated metadata such as dates, likes, post identifiers, source information, and classification labels.The dataset includes three label categories: HS0, HS1, and HSN, representing the dataset's original classification scheme. These labels can be used to investigate patterns in online discourse and develop or evaluate machine learning models for identifying potentially hateful or harmful content. The comments include informal language, transliterated Indian languages, and multilingual social media expressions, making the dataset potentially useful for studying language variation and the challenges of automated content moderation. The ContextGuard K2 Ready Dataset is a structured dataset designed for research into context-aware social media analysis, conversational language understanding, and automated content moderation. It contains 2,480 records represented by two columns: Input_Sequence and Target_Score. The Input_Sequence field uses a structured format containing [CONTEXT] and [TARGET] markers. It represents conversational context followed by a target comment or user-generated text. This structure enables research into how preceding messages may influence the interpretation and classification of subsequent content, particularly in discussions involving offensive language, abusive expressions, and potentially harmful online interactions.The Target_Score field contains numerical values of 0.0, 0.5, and 1.0. These scores provide a numerical target for supervised machine learning experiments. Their precise semantic interpretation should be established from the dataset's labeling methodology before assigning specific meanings to individual score values. The ContextGuard SFT Dataset V4 is a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) dataset developed for research and experimentation in automated content moderation, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and multilingual text classification. The dataset contains 760 structured training examples designed to train AI moderation systems to classify user-generated text into three categories: BENIGN, WARN, and ESCALATE.Each record follows a conversational message format consisting of a system instruction, a user-provided text sample, and an assistant response. The system instruction defines the moderation task and specifies the expected output structure. The assistant response contains a reasoning section enclosed intags, followed by a classification decision enclosed intags.The dataset includes Hinglish text and English-language social media comments, including informal expressions, offensive language, potentially harmful statements, and discussions requiring contextual interpretation. This makes it useful for investigating the challenges of moderation across informal, multilingual, and code-mixed language.

title: Holographic Neural Memory Architectures and Distributed Associative Networks: Phase-Encoded Interference, High-Dimensional Vector Representations, and Fault-Tolerant Recall
authors: Akash-B. Atapi, Man Mohit, Dr. Vishal Shrivastava, Dr. Vibhakar Pathak, Er. Amit Kumar Tiwari
abstract: Modern neural network architectures—ranging from deep transformers to recurrent networks—rely predominantly on localized, addressable weight matrices stored in physical RAM or high-bandwidth memory (HBM). While effective for general inference, localized memory architectures exhibit catastrophic fragility under random memory corruption, lack graceful degradation when subjected to hardware bit-flips, and scale inefficiently when forming distributed associative bindings across millions of abstract concepts. Holographic Neural Memory (HNM) and HighDimensional Vector Symbolic Architectures (VSA / Hyperdimensional Computing) establish a transformative non-local computing paradigm inspired by optical holography and distributed brain memory. By encoding symbolic information into high-dimensional hypervectors (d >= 10,000) via random orthogonal projections and superimposing associations through complex phase-encoded interference, HNM architectures distribute information uniformly across every spatial component of the memory vector. This superposition property grants remarkable fault tolerance: distributed associative memories can experience up to 45% total vector component corruption or hardware bit-erasure while still executing clean pattern completion, un-aliased retrieval, and robust compositional reasoning. However, scaling holographic memories to enterprise foundation models introduces severe computational and mathematical bottlenecks: noise accumulation and crosstalk interference during massive vector superpositions, dimensionality curse during multi-hop role-filler binding, and complex hardware mapping onto conventional von Neumann processors. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of holographic neural memory architectures. We formalize phase-encoded circular convolution binding, derive signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) capacity bounds under random hypervector superposition, and model fault-tolerant pattern recall. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise software and hardware-in-the-loop testbed evaluating holographic memory layers integrated with transformer residual streams across massive relational retrieval tasks, multi-modal concept grounding, and radiation-hardened edge aerospace workloads. Our empirical findings demonstrate that holographic neural memories achieve 99.2% robust associative recall under 40% random bit corruption, outperforming conventional hash tables and key-value caches by orders of magnitude in resilience, while sustaining sub-microsecond retrieval latencies on dedicated processing-in-memory (PIM) accelerators. Finally, we formulate open challenges in non-linear compositional generalization, continuous-time hypervector dynamics, and alloptical holographic processor hardware realization

title: ZAPP: a zero-aware photovoltaic power prediction framework
abstract: Predicting photovoltaic power generator outputs is not easy, especially when the values are near zero, because even very small errors can lead to large percentage errors. We introduce a new forecasting framework, ZAPP (Zero-Aware Photovoltaic Power Predictor), that handles near-zero errors while maintaining high prediction accuracy. The model does not rely on a single unified regression model but instead attaches two refinement stages to a base regression model. The first stage, called ZeroGate, predicts whether the output should be zero. The second refinement stage, the low-power MAPE reducer, fine-tunes the non-zero outputs near the zero level without significantly affecting scale-dependent regression metrics. The datasets are divided into training, validation, and test sets in chronological order, ensuring that test data is not used during model development, threshold tuning, ensemble weighting, or calibration. Experimental evaluation included base models such as Persistence, Ridge, XGBoost, LSTM, Transformer, and a hybrid Ridge–XGBoost model. Two separate datasets are employed to strengthen the quality of the results. For the hybrid model, sMAPE fell from 60.57% to 11.07% on Dataset 1. Its final MAE, RMSE, and R 2 were 22.37, 60.72, and 0.9637, respectively. On Dataset 2, sMAPE decreased from 63.30% to 11.92%, with MAE = 52.24, RMSE = 144.60, and R 2 = 0.9559. The zero-aware correction mainly reduced percentage errors without weakening the overall regression results.
