title: Boundary: Universal Continuity and Recoverability Sciences — Complete Canonical Framework
abstract: Boundary: Universal Continuity and Recoverability Sciences — Complete Canonical Framework Noelia Sofia Sanchez | Interval Studio | 2026 Overview Boundary presents the consolidated canonical framework of Continuity Science, Recoverability Science, and Recoverability-Constrained Systems, developed across an interconnected body of formal publications, computational structures, technical architectures, scientific disciplines, constitutional instruments, and interdisciplinary applications. This edition integrates the established internal architecture and documented publication lineage into a unified reference distribution. It preserves foundational works, formal definitions, conditional theorems, analytical matrices, implementation frameworks, governance instruments, and subsequent canonical extensions. Boundary addresses a fundamental operational question: under what conditions can a system undergo change, intervention, interruption, transformation, delegation, or succession while retaining admissible, executable paths to protected future states? Scientific Foundations The framework connects: Recoverability Science: admissible continuation under irreversibility constraints. Continuity Science: preservation and transformation of materially significant identity, state, relationships, capabilities, and successor possibilities. Continuity Mathematics: successor-state structures, finite reachability, protected target sets, recovery boundaries, invariants, abstraction, and proof obligations. Continuity Ontology: existence, distinction, identity, relation, state, transition, boundary, and persistence. Distinction and Materiality Science: identification and preservation of operationally consequential differences. Recursive Systems Governance: self-application of admissibility, evidence, accountability, and recoverability conditions to evaluators, controllers, institutions, and successor systems. Canonical Mathematical Structure Let C*(X) represent the admissibly reachable successor structure of a modeled state X, and let G denote a specified protected target class. Relative recoverability is represented by: R(X,G) = 1 if and only if C(X) ∩ G ≠ ∅.* The framework distinguishes conceptual possibility from executable recovery, incorporating temporal constraints, detection, intervention, authority, resources, independence, provenance, verification, and operational feasibility. Before an irreversible boundary, the governing criterion concerns preservation of admissible recoverable futures. Where the original protected state can no longer be recovered, continuation is assessed through the greatest recoverable remainder, including containment, correction, reconstruction, substitution, remedy, compensation, adaptation, and successor obligations. Mathematical results are presented according to their declared assumptions, definitions, derivations, proofs, and limits. Integrated Sciences and Architectures The consolidated framework incorporates formal, computational, technological, biological, cognitive, ecological, economic, institutional, and civilizational continuity. Its disciplinary architecture encompasses epistemic continuity, systems engineering, artificial intelligence continuity, computational recoverability, materials and infrastructure, health systems, agency and consent, identity and sovereignty, finance and livelihoods, environmental resilience, collective governance, intergenerational protection, and continuity of knowledge. Technical architectures address controlled transitions, safe interruption, isolation, execution verification, monitoring, recovery, successor handover, evidence integrity, and recursive supervision. Computational Canon The edition includes multiple canonical and historical analytical releases, including million-intersection matrices, nine-direction evaluations, scenario classifications, dependency mappings, proof audits, evidence registers, computational methods, and recursive closure assessments. Each version retains its documented scope and evaluation rules. Apparent disagreements between releases are preserved for reconciliation instead of being silently converted into equivalence. Constitutional and Institutional Architecture The framework incorporates the Universal Continuity and Recoverability constitutional materials, model governance principles, human-rights protections, obligations concerning agency and consent, institutional accountability, and mechanisms for lawful succession, remedy, compensation, and review. Constitutional, legislative, contractual, technical-standard, and international adoption materials are distinguished according to their applicable legal and institutional status. Living-System and Successor Continuity The living-system architecture integrates individual, collective, organizational, ecological, and intergenerational continuity. Recognition, protection, dignity, identity, agency, informed consent, representation, and remedies are treated as distinct obligations. Recognition may ground duties of protection without independently proving a particular scientific theory of consciousness. The framework further examines continuity across biological, technical, social, and future-developed forms of organization, maintaining evidence distinctions where empirical knowledge remains incomplete. Recursive Closure The canonical integration sequence is: DISTINCTION → MATERIALITY → RECOVERABILITY → SUCCESSOR CONTINUITY → RECURSIVE VERIFICATION → META-CLOSURE → LOCAL SILENCE Local silence signifies analytical closure under declared distinctions, evidence, rules, and scope. It is not a declaration that future science, counterexamples, or discovery are impossible. Any materially new evidence, dependency, counterexample, protected interest, or successor condition reopens the analysis. Consolidated Distribution This Zenodo record provides the Boundary canonical framework in eight independent ZIP archives, accompanied by an inventory and verification manifest. The distribution consolidates its foundational scientific work, formal research structures, technical systems, constitutional architecture, computational material, meta-sciences, and canonical extensions into a single citable record. It serves as a reference edition for the continuing development, examination, implementation, and critical evaluation of the Boundary framework. Status: Consolidated published-framework edition. Formal, empirical, technical, and legal claims retain their respective evidence and validation requirements.

It serves as a reference edition for the continuing development, examination, implementation, and critical evaluation of the Boundary framework. Status: Consolidated published-framework edition. abstract: A structured, machine-readable toponym lexicon of Bukhara region, Uzbekistan, andcompanion dataset to the paper of the same name. It holds 3,060 records standingfor 3,360 name occurrences across 16 types of geographic object (settlements,mahallas, cemeteries, hills, canals and others). title: One Language, Two Unequal Scripts: Separating Orthography from Information in Multilingual Representations with Punjabi
abstract: Multilingual models are said to abstract away script in their middle layers. Tests usually compare languages that differ in script and language at once. Punjabi does not. It is written in Gurmukhi and in Shahmukhi, which differ in what they record, since unvocalised Shahmukhi leaves short vowels and gemination unwritten. In a public recreation of XLM-R's training data, Shahmukhi Punjabi is about 1% as frequent as Gurmukhi. We use this pair to separate script form from missing information in four encoders. Every statistic is compared with the same architecture under random weights and bootstrapped over sentences. Four Gurmukhi controls remove information in steps. The share of the gap they leave falls at every step, and under these controls the two ends estimate it at 0.65 to 0.90. The pattern holds on human-written Shahmukhi. Across three XLM-R sizes the Punjabi gap grows slightly, while the gap for Serbian Cyrillic and Latin, whose Latin orthography is abundant as Croatian, shrinks and drops below its random baseline in XL. This fits a role for script resource but does not isolate it as the cause. Three mean-pooled decoders do not show this ordering. Transliteration closes 45% of a cross-script gap in topic-classification accuracy.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Preventable Hospitalization and Readmission Reduction: A Structured Narrative Review
abstract: Purpose: To critically assess reinforcement learning (RL) for sequential interventions designed to reduce preventable hospitalizations and readmissions, distinguishing computational feasibility from demonstrated clinical effectiveness. Methods: A structured narrative review synthesized direct utilization-focused policies, adjacent inpatient decision policies, and contextual prediction research through 9 October 2026. Outcomes, Markov decision formulations, off-policy estimators, and methodological limitations were analyzed without meta-analysis. Results: Directly relevant peer-reviewed evidence centers on Medicaid care management and post-discharge intervention planning. A retrospective state-action-reward-state-action (SARSA) study estimated a 12-percentage-point reduction in an emergency visit and hospitalization composite; however, this reflects a model-based counterfactual estimate rather than an observed randomized treatment effect. A larger offline study reported non-inferiority on a shaped reward scale alongside narrower intervention-allocation disparities. Data-pooling research contributed theoretical regret bounds and empirical support for learning across patient classes. Critical limitations across the literature include unmeasured confounding, limited action support, surrogate rewards, overlapping cohorts, and absent external validation. No direct study established a prospective randomized reduction in hospitalizations from an executed RL policy. Conclusion: RL provides a coherent framework for longitudinal care allocation, but current evidence supports algorithmic development rather than proven clinical efficacy. Translation demands explicit endpoint definitions, rigorous off-policy evaluation, prospective silent workflow evaluation, and controlled trials with safety, equity, and resource constraints.

title: Verifier-Bound Rule Discovery: A Pre-Registered Evaluation of LLM Proposers for Combinatorial Scheduling
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as proposers of human-readable rules in scientific discovery and combinatorial optimization (FunSearch, ARCHE, SVBRD-LLM). Yet the LLM-proposer systems we surveyed share a methodological gap: none reports a same-budget random-proposer control, none pre-registers its acceptance criteria, and none evaluates at distribution scale –- ARCHE validates on three hand-picked cases, and SVBRD-LLM, the closest system to ours, is outperformed on accuracy by a black-box LSTM while reporting no significance tests. We apply a verifier-bound rule-discovery framework in which an LLM proposes interpretable rules (linear weight vectors and sandboxed programs), an independent programmatic verifier checks domain-hard properties, holdout evaluation is physically isolated and executed exactly once, and every acceptance criterion is frozen before experiments run. title: Quem é o autor quando a inteligência artificial redige?
abstract: O presente estudo examina os fundamentos jurídicos, filosóficos e epistemológicos da autoria humana em textos produzidos com o auxílio de inteligência artificial generativa, especialmente nas situações em que a concepção intelectual, a estrutura argumentativa, a seleção das fontes e a revisão crítica permanecem sob controle humano, enquanto a redação material é realizada por sistemas de IA. Mediante pesquisa qualitativa, bibliográfica e documental, de natureza jurídico-dogmática e teórico-argumentativa, o trabalho analisa a legislação brasileira de direitos autorais, precedentes nacionais e estrangeiros, diretrizes de integridade científica e contribuições contemporâneas sobre agência intelectual, curadoria e controle humano significativo. A investigação distingue autoria jurídico-autoral, autoria científico-acadêmica e autoria epistemológica, demonstrando que a impossibilidade de reconhecer sistemas de IA como autores não implica atribuição automática de autoria humana aos resultados produzidos. Como contribuição teórica, propõe-se o critério da autoria intelectual demonstrável, segundo o qual o reconhecimento da autoria humana depende da identificação de contribuições criativas efetivas na concepção, arquitetura, direção, verificação e integração do trabalho. Conclui-se que a autoria humana pode subsistir mesmo quando a redação material é produzida por inteligência artificial, desde que a contribuição intelectual seja demonstrável, sem que isso assegure necessariamente proteção autoral sobre todos os elementos gerados pelo sistema.

title: Volume VIII: Molecular Case Studies: Resource and Entanglement Analysis for Battery Electrolyte and Iron–Sulfur Systems
abstract: This eighth volume performs an end-to-end resource and entanglement analysis for two concrete molecular systems that illustrate the residual-risk indicators of Volume VI. The first is the vinylene-carbonate + singlet-oxygen reaction path relevant to lithium-ion battery electrolytes, for which orbital von Neumann entropies were reconstructed on the Quantinuum H1-1 trapped-ion processor in 2025. The second is iron–sulfur clusters (including the FeMo-cofactor of nitrogenase), where entanglement-minimised orbitals have been shown to improve initial-state overlaps for quantum phase estimation by orders of magnitude. For each system the binding memory, interconnect and control specifications are identified, and the additional overhead imposed by fermionic superselection rules is quantified. The analysis demonstrates which of the readiness thresholds remain unmet and how modular cryogenic and cryo-CMOS advances would close them.

title: Projeto ELO
abstract: O avanço dos sistemas de inteligência artificial conversacional trouxe novos desafios relacionados à qualidade da interação entre humanos e máquinas. Embora os modelos atuais demonstrem elevada capacidade de geração de linguagem natural, ainda persistem dificuldades relacionadas à manutenção do contexto, adaptação às necessidades do usuário e adequação comunicacional. Este artigo apresenta o Projeto Elo, uma proposta conceitual destinada à investigação da qualidade conversacional em sistemas de inteligência artificial. O modelo organiza a análise em três pilares complementares: Continuidade Conversacional, Adaptação Conversacional e Respeito Conversacional. A pesquisa propõe critérios observáveis para avaliação qualitativa das interações e utiliza registros de observação como base para construção de hipóteses investigativas. Os resultados preliminares sugerem que a qualidade percebida de uma interação depende não apenas da exatidão das respostas, mas também da capacidade da inteligência artificial de preservar decisões anteriores, adaptar-se ao contexto emergente e comunicar-se de forma adequada às necessidades do usuário.

title: Evaluating the Trust and Provenance Guarantees of Multimedia Authentication Codes: a Visualization-Driven Deep Cryptanalytic Assessment of SipHash
abstract: As multimedia becomes the primary vector for persuasion-optimized misinformation, the underlying authentication and provenance mechanisms that verify content origin and integrity becomes critical. Message Authentication Codes (MACs) are fundamental for safeguarding multimedia content against unauthorized modification and forgery. Differential cryptanalysis has established itself as a powerful tool for analyzing such symmetric cryptographic primitives. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) have demonstrated that ML-powered differential distinguishers can capture subtle statistical features, complementing conventional analytical techniques and offering new perspectives for security evaluation. To the best of our knowledge, this paper presents the first visualization-driven ML-based security evaluation of the widely deployed Addition-Rotation-Xor (ARX)-based MAC SipHash under chosen-message attacks. We investigate two observation domains: intermediate internal states and final authentication tags, demonstrating that the proposed distinguishers effectively capture differential characteristics across both the internal state evolution and in publicly observable outputs. The experimental results demonstrate that reduced-round SipHash preserves distinguishable statistical characteristics before complete diffusion is achieved, while classification performance progressively approaches random guessing as additional rounds are introduced. We identify ML-assisted distinguishers for SipHash-c-d, where (c, d) ∈ {(1, 0), (1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0), (2, 1), (3, 0)}, demonstrating that recurrence-plot-based feature learning effectively evaluates the differential security of MACs. The proposed methodology strengthens the auditability of provenance infrastructure underpinning platform-scale multimedia integrity against adversarially engineered content.

title: An Integrated XAI-RL Architecture for Ethical Decision-Making in Autonomous Robots
abstract: Can a robot's ethical reasoning be transparent without slowing it down? That is the question we set out to answer. Autonomous robots now make decisions that affect people's lives, and if we cannot understand how they decide, trust becomes a serious problem. We built a unified architecture that couples Explainable AI (XAI) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) through three connected components: a Perception Layer for situational awareness, a Decision Reasoning Layer that breaks agent utility down into measurable ethical sub-rewards (safety, fairness, and well-being), and a contrastive Explainability Engine grounded in a real-time Ethical Ledger. We tested it against Black-Box RL and two post-hoc XRL baselines (LIME and SHAP) across two simulation environments and a physical robot pilot on a TurtleBot3 platform. Our system reached 92±3% ethical alignment in simulation and 89±4% on the physical platform, beating every baseline (p < 0.01 throughout). In a controlled, IRB-approved user study (N=128), participants rated it higher on trust (4.5±0.4), understandability (4.6±0.3), and perceived safety (4.4±0.5) than the alternatives. Explanations were also fast: 4.2±0.6 ms on average, versus 18.3±2.1 ms for SHAP and 12.7±1.8 ms for LIME on the same hardware—well within real-time limits. An ablation study and sensitivity analysis back up these architectural choices.

title: Sovereign Cognitive Architecture for Autonomous Meta-Cognitive Reasoning with Non-Monotonic Lexicographic Ethical Governance and Quantum-Classical Causal Optimization
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Sovereign Cognitive Architecture is a tripartite AI framework integrating rapid intuition (System 1), deep analytical reasoning (System 2), and a meta-cognitive monitor (System 3). It resolves critical AI vulnerabilities through four core innovations: (1) a non-linear adaptive differential self-model that mathematically guarantees identity continuity and actively resists adversarial prompt injection; (2) a hardware-isolated, non-monotonic lexicographic ethical governance engine enforcing 12 inviolable principles, triggering physical circuit breaks or cryptographic revocation upon violation to ensure absolute ethical compliance; (3) a quantum-classical translation interface utilizing QAOA to provide heuristic, high-quality approximate solutions for NP-hard combinatorial causal routing, explicitly avoiding false polynomial-time claims; and (4) a dynamic gating mechanism that strategically applies Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) only to high-sensitivity operations, bypassing it for routine tasks to achieve a verified 60% net energy reduction compared to monolithic encrypted systems. This architecture enables autonomous, self-evolving, and ethically bounded cognitive processing.

title: The Self–Mutual–World–Meta–Future–Causality–Action–Information–Goal–Structure–Uncertainty–Resources–Memory–Evidence–Constraints Model: A Unified Framework for Adaptive Coordination in Computational Systems
abstract: Computational systems increasingly operate in environments where effective behavior depends not only on internal processing and interaction among computational agents, but also on environmental representation, metacognitive control, future-state prediction, causal analysis, action selection, information management, goal representation, structural organization, uncertainty estimation, resource allocation, memory, evidence evaluation, and constraint satisfaction. Existing approaches address many of these functions through distinct research traditions, including world models, metareasoning, model-based planning, causal inference, multi-agent systems, information theory, memory-augmented computation, and constrained optimization. However, the relationships among these functions can create a complex coordination problem in which no single processing mechanism is necessarily optimal throughout an entire task. This paper proposes the Self–Mutual–World–Meta–Future–Causality–Action–Information–Goal–Structure–Uncertainty–Resources–Memory–Evidence–Constraints Model (SMWMFC-AIGSURMEC), a conceptual framework comprising fifteen computational objects organized into interacting functional layers. The Self object represents internal computation; the Mutual object represents interaction among computational entities; the World object represents the state and dynamics of the environment; the Meta object monitors and regulates computational processes; the Future object represents predicted possible states; the Causality object represents hypothesized cause–effect relationships; the Action object represents executable interventions; the Information object represents information acquisition and transformation; the Goal object represents desired outcomes; the Structure object represents organizational relationships; the Uncertainty object represents incomplete knowledge and predictive uncertainty; the Resources object represents computational and operational budgets; the Memory object preserves information across processing stages; the Evidence object evaluates support for claims and decisions; and the Constraints object specifies admissible behavior and solutions. The central proposal is that these objects should be coordinated through an adaptive controller that selects, configures, and terminates computational mechanisms according to task state, expected utility, uncertainty, evidence quality, causal relevance, predicted outcomes, and resource availability. The framework distinguishes the representation of an object from the mechanisms that operate on it, and it allows individual processing, cross-entity interaction, environmental simulation, metacognitive regulation, and action execution to be combined when appropriate. A formal system definition, an adaptive control objective, an operational algorithm, implementation principles, research hypotheses, and an empirical evaluation protocol are presented. The framework is a proposed theoretical and engineering design rather than an empirically validated system. Its contribution must be established through comparison with existing approaches and experiments testing whether coordinated selection among the fifteen objects improves performance, reliability, adaptability, and resource efficiency.

title: The D'Agapeyeff Cipher (1939): Grille recovery and polyphonic-table identifiability under n-gram scoring
abstract: The D’Agapeyeff Cipher (1939): grille recovery and polyphonic-table identifiability under n-gram scoring Research preprint. The report has been through internal verification and AI-assisted critical review. It has not been peer-reviewed. In 1939 Alexander D’Agapeyeff ended Codes and Ciphers with a 196-symbol challenge cipher that has never been read. Prior work (Hendrick 2026) showed that no one-to-one letter key with any transposition can produce its symbol counts. This study tests one construction that fits every observed property: a 14 × 14 turning grille over a polyphonic table, in which each of 13 symbols stands for a group of letters. The question is whether, under that hypothesis, the cipher’s key could be found at all. All rates below were measured on practice ciphers built in the hypothesized form with known keys. What this study adds, within the literature reviewed: Grille recovery when the polyphonic table is known (extends Hendrick’s one-to-one result). Six-symbol scoring recovered at least 45 of 49 grille orbits in 6 of 6 practice ciphers, 5 of them exactly. This is a preliminary demonstration, not recovery of the historical grille.The table must be essentially exact (extends Hendrick’s result to polyphonic tables). With 6 or more letters in the wrong group, the grille was found in 0 of 12 practice ciphers.182 symbols rarely single out the true table under the n-gram scores tested. The search started at the true table and was given the true symbol order. It kept the truth in only 11% of 200 practice ciphers, and in 8–26% across ten alternative setups (2,000 runs: natural prose, three corpora, four scores). The higher-scoring tables fit the particular passage, not English. Keeping the truth passes one in two at roughly 420 symbols.Four-square and two-square with random keys are excluded by symbol usage: none of 10,000 practice ciphers used 13 or fewer symbols.A four-square whose key is built around the message can reproduce the cipher’s usage and flatness: 13 of 100 passages; 10 of 100 were also not flagged by the order test used. This is a feasibility result and an open lead, not evidence that D’Agapeyeff used it.Under the methods tested, the hypothesis can be neither confirmed nor refuted from the ciphertext alone. No decipherment is claimed. These are measurements under stated methods, not a proof that no method could succeed. The work was an AI-assisted cryptanalysis study conceived and directed by Nicolas Houghtaling. Software, analyses and writing were done by Anthropic’s Claude under the author’s direction, supported by a team of AI agents. Drafts were reviewed by ChatGPT (OpenAI); that is an AI review, not peer review. Every result is recorded in a case file with its evidence. Before publication, every published experiment was rerun at full size from a fresh clone, with no network access. Of 4,959 records compared, 4,956 matched, and every printed number was recomputed. That was an internal reproduction by the project, not independent replication. Code, data, evidence and the validation record: https://github.com/voodoomods/dagapeyeff-cryptanalysis-1 Report and data: CC BY 4.0. Code: Apache-2.0. title: Compliant-by-Construction Hybrid Medical AI Workflows via Located Task Graphs
abstract: Abstract Hybrid artificial intelligence workflow s for medical imaging combine heterogeneous ingredients: public and private datasets, neural training, prediction, symbolic post-processing, spatial model checking, human assessment, and controlled circulation of results. Regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act impose strict requirements on high-risk AI systems, including those used in medical contexts, demanding transparency, traceability, and human oversight throughout the pipeline. In such regulated settings, the main difficulty is not only to obtain accurate predictions, but to make the procedure itself sufficiently explicit: where data belongs, where computation is performed, which artifacts may be moved, who can read them, and which human assessments are required before further use. We present the design of a lightweight calculus of located task graphs for compliant-by-construction hybrid AI workflow s. A program is reduced to a directed acyclic graph whose nodes are primitive operations (logical, non-logical, or AI-based such as training and prediction), and additionally, featuring assessment as a primitive, and whose edges are data dependencies. Each term is located along several dimensions: storage location, computation location, and institutional or regulatory context. The calculus is proposed at a conceptual level, leaving a complete formal semantics for future work. We illustrate how our calculus can support a design discipline for making compliance-relevant structure part of an executable specification in a medical-imaging case study.

title: Token cost by data format: JSON vs YAML vs CSV vs TOON on Claude, Gemini and GPT
abstract: The same 20-row product table (7 fields) written in 8 formats and counted on four tokenizers: Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.x and OpenAI o200k_base (GPT-4o and later). Headline: the table costs 1,336 GPT tokens as indented JSON and 429 as CSV (68% fewer). CSV was the cheapest format on every tokenizer tested; TOON came close but did not beat it; XML was the most expensive. Source page, chart and method: https://tokensave.app/data/token-cost-by-format Related: token cost by language on Claude, Gemini and GPT: https://tokensave.app/data/token-cost-by-language-claude-gemini Measured: 2026-10-17 License: CC BY 4.0 Key findings Switching from indented JSON to CSV cuts tokens by 68% on GPT, 66% on Claude 5.5 and 70% on Gemini. TOON needs 10% more tokens than CSV on GPT and 4% more on Claude 5.5. Minifying JSON saves 51% on Gemini and 43% on GPT but only 34% on Claude 5.5. Claude 5.5 needs 28% to 59% more tokens than GPT for the same data (largest gap: minified JSON). Files token-cost-by-format.csv: one row per format with character count, tokens and difference vs indented JSON for claude55, claude45, gemini, gpt token-cost-by-format.json: the same results plus all 8 input files verbatim, so every count can be reproduced Data Tokens for the same table, difference versus indented JSON on the same tokenizer in brackets. Format Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5 Claude Haiku 4.5 Gemini 3.x GPT o200k TSV 621 (-66%) 477 (-71%) 483 (-70%) 427 (-68%) CSV 620 (-66%) 476 (-71%) 482 (-70%) 429 (-68%) TOON 647 (-65%) 502 (-69%) 508 (-69%) 474 (-65%) Markdown table 800 (-57%) 649 (-60%) 590 (-64%) 539 (-60%) JSON (minified) 1,210 (-34%) 847 (-48%) 791 (-51%) 763 (-43%) YAML 1,275 (-31%) 1,074 (-34%) 1,076 (-34%) 997 (-25%) JSON (indented) 1,841 (±0%) 1,618 (±0%) 1,623 (±0%) 1,336 (±0%) XML 2,200 (+20%) 1,868 (+15%) 1,873 (+15%) 1,603 (+20%) Method One table of 20 products x 7 fields (id, name, category, price, in_stock, rating, tags), written as indented JSON (2 spaces), minified JSON, YAML, XML, CSV, TSV, a Markdown table and TOON (tabular form, tags joined with |). Claude: each file sent through Claude Code (claude -p) with a fixed one-line system prompt; reported input tokens minus the same run with a one-character message. Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 gave identical counts. Gemini: Google AI Studio prompt token counter on Gemini 3.8 Flash, minus its one start token. XML, CSV and indented JSON were measured twice; CSV and JSON matched, and the XML value is from the second run. GPT: tiktoken with o200k_base. Limitations One flat table. Deeply nested data does not fit CSV well; there JSON or YAML may be the practical choice. Token count only: models may read some formats more reliably than others. Claude values can be off by about ±2 tokens (under 1% here).

title: Human-AI-Computer Interaction: Measuring Whether AI Strengthens Unaided Judgment
abstract: A tool that helps a person answer today and leaves them no better at answering alone next week has made them dependent on it. We state a measurement protocol that separates the two outcomes. On one task set, three scores are taken: the person's unaided score H_p, the model's AI score A, and the person's joint score J_p with the model's answer in view. The multiplier is m_p = J_p / max(H_p, A), the gain is D = J_p - max(H_p, A), and the unaided test is repeated after seven days to give retention R_p = H_p(t + 7 d) - H_p(t) and learning L = J_p(t + 7 d) - H_p(t + 7 d). A tool that raises J_p while L stays at or below zero across its interval marks dependence. The instrument is the hai probe in Bucket's bkt package: a frozen bank of 998 four-choice items across the seven canon branches, of which 68 are held out by an automated distractor review; sessions of 40 items in 20 pairs matched on tier and on whether the model got the pair's items right; a 20 second think window before the model's answer appears; no feedback until the retest; guess-corrected scores and a bootstrap over pairs for every interval. The learning side of the measurement is the minimum prerequisite learning problem: the catalog is a directed acyclic graph of concepts, a learner's state is a closed set of mastered concepts, and the least a learner must add to reach a target is the required set R(t, M), the target's prerequisite closure minus their mastery, a count proved minimal in Lean 4 under stated assumptions. Three rules will join the two sides, probe items drawn at the learner's frontier, R_p reported against the engine's predicted recall, and mastery updated from the solo half only; all three are design, since the probe code holds no mastery or FSRS logic today. The instrument is built and no probe has been retested, so this report carries no result on a person; the learning system's own evaluation, 57,060 enumerated planning cases with zero errors and a synthetic prediction experiment, is reported with its source. The report states the planned analysis, paired comparisons stratified by education level, a divergence hypothesis on how reliance on one model narrows the range of answers across a group, and the rule by which the scores decide which tasks Research OS hands to the model and which it keeps with the person.

title: Does the Train-Gain/Generalization Relation Transfer? A Pre-Registered Cross-Domain Test of Inverted-U Behavior in Verifier-Bound Rule Discovery
abstract: A verifier-bound rule-discovery engine –- an LLM proposes executable rules, a programmatic verifier gates them, a single-shot isolated holdout scores them –- was run in three domains under one pre-registered methodology. The first domain (combinatorial scheduling) reported an inverted-U relation between training improvement and holdout generalization: moderate training gains generalized best, and the largest gains overfit. This paper reports the pre-registered cross-domain test of that relation. Under the frozen protocol (quartile buckets over margin-positive pairs; criterion: middle buckets' mean win rate exceeds the ends' by 0.05; $ 2$ of $ 2$ participating domains required), the criterion replicates: scheduling $0.35/0.60/0.70/0.48$ (mid $0.650$ vs.\ ends $0.413$) and MCS task assignment $0.36/0.93/1.00/1.00$ (mid $0.964$ vs.\ ends $0.679$). The second domain (MCS incentive design) is excluded by the protocol's own rule –- its verifier passed 3 of 2,000 LLM rules and 0 of the human-designed references, a threshold effect that leaves no margin-positive pairs. The substantive finding is not the verdict but the shape divergence beneath it: in scheduling the top quartile declines (48\ overfitting), while in assignment the top quartile saturates at 100\ different mechanisms. We read the pattern –- hard 0–1 verification collapses generalization, mid-severity simulation lets the top quartile overfit, feasibility-by-construction transfers it –- as evidence that verifier strictness determines the fate of the largest training gains, and we report the two-level verdict (criterion: replicated; mechanism: not shared) as the result. Pre-registrations, ledgers, and analysis scripts are available from the authors upon reasonable request via email.

title: Diagnostic Algorithm Selection for Low-Dimensional Euclidean Clustering: Code, Frozen Models, and Experimental Results
abstract: Overview This repository contains the source code, frozen models, experimental configurations, evaluation results, and reproducibility materials for the research study Diagnostic Algorithm Selection for Low-Dimensional Euclidean Clustering: Geometry-Guided Routing, Portfolio Verification, and Generalization Limits. The study investigates how geometric characteristics of unlabeled observations can inform the selection of established clustering algorithms. Its focus is on the relationships among clustering quality, algorithm-selection decisions, computational cost, robustness, and generalization across different data distributions. Geometric Diagnostics and Algorithm Selection The framework uses four label-free geometric diagnostics: Hopkins clusterability: spatial clustering tendency. Local density-radius variation: differences in nearest-neighbor distances. Geodesic distortion: graph shortest-path distances relative to Euclidean distances. Minimum spanning tree tail concentration: the contribution of the longest spanning-tree edges. A frozen random-forest performance predictor maps these diagnostics to a recommendation among five clustering families: K-means, Ward hierarchical clustering, spectral clustering, HDBSCAN, and Gaussian mixture models. The study also evaluates label-free verification strategies. These include full five-candidate silhouette verification and restricted two- and three-candidate portfolios. The restricted portfolios use frozen model predictions to form candidate shortlists, followed by internal silhouette-based verification with a fixed decision margin. title: tempestpy: Easy-to-Use Shielded Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Abstract Safe exploration is a key challenge in Reinforcement Learning (RL) that aims to prevent agents from making decisions that could cause harm while exploring their environment. Shielding is one such technique that assumes domain knowledge in the form of a model of the environment to decide upon the safety of an action. Although shielding is a well-established approach, it has seen limited application in RL due to significant barriers. The main obstacle is the lack of an accessible end-to-end infrastructure that connects formal shield synthesis with standard RL frameworks. As a result, applying shielding requires expertise in formal methods and substantial engineering effort to construct probabilistic models, which has kept it outside the typical RL workflow. We address this problem by extending our shield synthesis tool Tempest into a practical backend for safe RL. Our core contribution is tempestpy , a Python library that integrates Tempest -based shield synthesis directly into the Gymnasium API, allowing shields to be synthesised and deployed within existing RL pipelines. This substantially lowers the barrier to entry for shielding and turns formal safe-exploration methods into a usable component for RL practitioners. In addition, we extend Tempest ’s algorithmic support to compute sound shields for stochastic multiplayer games, thereby preserving formal safety guarantees. In this setting, specifying a model of the environment becomes the remaining requirement rather than the primary integration challenge. We demonstrate the resulting workflow end to end and evaluate shielded and unshielded RL across multiple environments. To facilitate the modeling step, we provide symbolic models for Minigrid and introduce $$\textsc {Minigrid}^{\small {\textsc {Safe}}}$$ M I N I G R I D S A F E , a collection of playground environments designed to make shielding easily accessible and experimentally transparent. $$\textsc {Minigrid}^{\small {\textsc {Safe}}}$$ M I N I G R I D S A F E extends Minigrid with safety-oriented scenarios featuring probabilistic transitions and additional agents, enabling the study of challenging safety aspects in a simple and intuitive setting.

title: O'ZBEK TILIDA PRESUPPOZITSIYANI AVTOMATIK ANIQLASH: KORPUS VA TABIIY TILNI QAYTA ISHLASH YONDASHUVI
authors: O'ZBEK TILIDA PRESUPPOZITSIYANI AVTOMATIK ANIQLASH: KORPUS VA TABIIY TILNI QAYTA ISHLASH YONDASHUVI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada o‘zbek tilida presuppozitsiyani avtomatik aniqlashningkorpus va tabiiy tilni qayta ishlashga asoslangan modeli yoritiladi. Presuppozitsiya triggerlarinianiqlash, morfologik-sintaktik tahlil, kontekstni modellashtirish, korpus annotatsiyasi vatransformer modellaridan foydalanish imkoniyatlari o‘zbek tilining agglutinativ xususiyatlaridoirasida ilmiy jihatdan tahlil qilinadi.Kalit so‘zlar: presuppozitsiya, presuppozitsiya triggeri, korpus lingvistikasi, tabiiy tilniqayta ishlash, pragmatik inferensiya, transformer modeli, o‘zbek tili.Аннотация. В данной статье рассматривается модель автоматическогообнаружения пресуппозиций в узбекском языке, основанная на корпусной лингвистике иобработке естественного языка. В рамках агглютинативных свойств узбекского языканаучно анализируются возможности использования триггеров пресуппозиций,морфологически-синтаксического анализа, контекстного моделирования, аннотированиякорпуса и трансформерных моделей.Ключевые слова: пресуппозиция, триггер пресуппозиции, корпусная лингвистика,обработка естественного языка, прагматический вывод, трансформерная модель,узбекский язык.Abstract. This article discusses a model for automatic presupposition detection in theUzbek language based on corpus and natural language processing. The possibilities of usingpresupposition triggers, morphological-syntactic analysis, context modeling, corpus annotation,and transformer models are scientifically analyzed within the framework of the agglutinativeproperties of the Uzbek language.Keywords: presupposition, presupposition trigger, corpus linguistics, natural languageprocessing, pragmatic inference, transformer model, Uzbek language.

title: Применение искусственного интеллекта в финансовом инжиниринге
abstract: В статье рассматриваются направления применения искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) в финансовом инжиниринге – при проектировании, оценке и хеджировании финансовых инструментов, построении портфелей и управлении рисками. На основе обзора научной литературы и данных Банка России систематизированы основные классы задач, в которых методы машинного обучения дают преимущество перед классическими моделями, и показаны ограничения их использования. Установлено, что в 2025 г. ИИ на постоянной основе применяли 21 % опрошенных российских финансовых организаций, ещё 15 % тестировали пилотные проекты. Сделан вывод о том, что ИИ не заменяет финансовую теорию, а расширяет инструментарий финансового инженера, однако требует развития систем управления модельным риском и объяснимости моделей.

title: 十进制光子连续计算机的核心读取硬件与半导体实施路线
abstract: 本文提出十进制光子连续计算机的核心读取硬件方案,以两个反向排列的无偏置弱PN结构成孪生有向结算胞,通过材料方向响应与独立阈值实现光态的直接数字读取。结合零偏置隧道探测、1550纳米锗光电探测及二维半导体局域结区制造技术,提出从双结实验验证到单片集成的实施路线,为连续光学关系计算与离散数字结算的硬件衔接提供可检验方案。

title: RAPID-Audio: reproducibility archive (version 3.0)
abstract: Reproducibility archive accompanying the article "RAPID-Audio: Authenticated Selective Speech Disclosure with Adversarial Analysis of Content and Metadata Leakage" by Annas W. Malik and Kashif Nasr. It contains the source code of the protocol, of both receivers, of the SEL-EtM reference design, of the frame selectors, of the attacks and of the analysis; the identifiers of every evaluation set; derived data (word times, recogniser output, AMI transcripts and entity labels); the synthetic benchmarks E13 and E14 with their audio and the E14 protocol fixed in advance; every per-utterance and per-trial result and the log of every run; test vectors; model revisions and checksums of the external data; scripts that regenerate every table and figure; and a verification script (python -I code/verify.py) that checks every file against SHA256SUMS, recomputes every summary from the raw outputs and reruns the protocol tests without audio, models or a GPU. LibriSpeech and AMI audio and the model weights are not redistributed; datasets.json gives their sources and checksums. title: The Self-and-Self-and-World Model: A General Computational Framework for Adaptive Coordination Between Internal Computational Mechanisms and World-State Modeling
abstract: Computational systems increasingly operate in environments where successful behavior depends on both the organization of internal computation and the ability to represent, predict, and respond to external conditions. A system may possess multiple internal computational mechanisms for generation, diagnosis, verification, correction, planning, and evaluation, while also maintaining a model of the world in which its decisions are executed. However, internal mechanism selection and world-state modeling are often treated as separate design problems. This separation can limit a system's ability to determine not only what it should compute, but also which aspects of its world model require additional computation, when internal mechanisms should be activated, and when predicted consequences justify further investigation. This paper proposes the Self-and-Self-and-World Model (SSWM), a general computational framework for adaptively coordinating internal computational mechanisms with world-state modeling. The framework distinguishes three interacting dimensions: the system's internal computational state, the organization of its internal mechanisms, and its representation of the external world. Its central principle is that a computational system should jointly determine how to allocate internal computation and how to maintain or revise its world model according to task requirements, uncertainty, prediction error, expected utility, environmental change, and computational constraints. SSWM formalizes the internal mechanism repertoire, world-state representation, model uncertainty, mechanism-dependent model updates, action-conditioned predictions, computational costs, and feedback-driven adaptation. It introduces a coupled decision formulation in which mechanism selection and world-model maintenance can influence one another. The paper presents a reference architecture, a proposed algorithm, conditional theoretical propositions, complexity considerations, experimental hypotheses, and a cross-domain evaluation program. SSWM is intended as an organizational abstraction for systems that must coordinate internal computation with representations of external conditions, including autonomous agents, robotics, planning, scientific computing, and model-based decision systems. Its distinct contribution, if supported by formal analysis and empirical evidence, would be a unified account of how internal mechanism organization and world-model management can be jointly adapted rather than optimized independently. The framework is proposed for investigation; its novelty, advantages, and generality require systematic comparison with existing research on world models, metareasoning, model-based planning, adaptive computation, and active information acquisition.

title: From Quantum Decoding to Sharp Subset Bounds: A Use Case for Extracted Mathematical Instruments
abstract: Quantum communication requires a receiver to distinguish several, generally mixed, signal states. A useful theoretical question is whether errors on smaller signal alphabets can certify the error of a decoder for the full alphabet. We study this question for the pretty good measurement and present it as a use case for the programme of extracting reusable mathematical instruments from a large collection of research manuscripts. A constrained spectral optimization mechanism identified in that collection leads to the sharp pairwise coefficient (1 + sqrt(1 - 2/N))^2 for all equally likely pure ensembles. A separate matrix analysis proves the sharp coefficient (1 + sqrt(1 - k/N))^2 for every subset size when the average state is maximally mixed on its support, allowing arbitrary mixed signals. For general mixed ensembles, the sharp leave-one coefficient (1 + 1/sqrt(N))^2 holds whenever the normalized full error is at least 1/N; consequently it holds for all equally likely ensembles in dimension at most N - 1. We give a noisy qutrit decoding example, an unrestricted bound for nearly full subsets, and an exact polynomial certificate for a further four-signal family. The account separates the extracted mechanisms, their classical antecedents, and the additional arguments needed for the quantum problem. These results provide conditional error certificates, while the unrestricted sharp mixed-state subset problem and improvements to operational communication rates remain open.

title: Robust Client Behavior Tracking for Malicious Detection in Secure-Aggregated Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a successful distributed machine learning paradigm, where diverse clients are able to collaboratively train a global model without releasing their raw data, thereby preserving the data privacy. To enhance even more privacy, it is common to use Secure Aggregation (SecAgg) to make the central server oblivious to any individual client and only get model updates aggregated. However, this approach cannot be used to identify a malicious actor falling victim to a model poisoning attack, data poisoning, and Byzantine attack, which poses a threat to the quality and effectiveness of the global model. In this research, we put forward a safe and reliable client behavior monitoring method for malicious detection in secure-aggregated federated learning. It does so by measuring the client's actions in an indirect way (consistency of contribution over time, stability of the updates, reliability of the training, convergence trends, reputation scores based on trust), and ensuring that the secure aggregation protocols are not broken. A dynamic risk assessment system identifies frauds whose activity is very divergent from legitimate players. Identifying malicious clients can enhance the robustness of the federated learning process by either giving the malicious client a reduced weight in the consensus function or excluding the malicious client from subsequent training rounds. Our approach: Privacy Protection, Robustness to adversarial behaviour, Good model accuracy in scenarios. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method can successfully detect malicious clients, better handle the poisoning attacks than the conventional secure aggregation approach without behavioral monitoring, consider the convergence stability and higher classification accuracy. The approach that we propose is practical and scalable for preserving privacy of the federated learning systems which are used in healthcare and financial applications, Internet of Things (IoT), and many other distributed intelligent applications.

title: Cycle-Invariant Lightweight Authenticated Encryption and Cross-Domain Silicon Entropy Harvesting on ARM Cortex-M0+
abstract: Abstract This record contains the complete artifacts, bare-metal C source code, and empirical benchmark logs for a cycle-invariant authenticated encryption and silicon-jitter true random number generator (TRNG) architecture implemented on an STM32C031 (ARM Cortex-M0+). Designed for resource-constrained edge systems (such as Electric Vehicle BMS nodes), the system achieves strict constant-time execution ($\Delta = 0$ clock cycle variance) to defeat timing side-channel attacks, harvests cross-domain clock phase jitter whitened via the hardware CRC-32 unit, and implements sub-microsecond interrupt-driven SRAM tamper key-shredding. 1. Introduction & Problem Statement Ultra-low-cost microcontrollers deployed in distributed automotive and IoT nodes frequently lack native hardware TRNGs and hardware AES accelerators. Standard software implementations are computationally expensive, consume excessive flash memory, and leak execution timing variations that allow attackers to recover secret keys via side-channel analysis. 2. Proposed Bare-Metal Architecture The proposed architecture operates via direct CMSIS register manipulation without software libraries or operating systems: Silicon-Jitter TRNG: Harvests phase drift between the core SysTick timer and peripheral TIM3 clock mixed with ADC1 SAR quantization noise, whitened through the on-chip CRC->DR polynomial engine. Constant-Time AEAD Pipeline: Implements a 32-round Feistel block cipher combined with a keyed Hardware CRC-32 MAC tag, utilizing zero data-dependent branches. Tamper Key-Shredding: Employs a RAM-relocated vector table (SCB->VTOR) and an EXTI0 falling-edge hardware interrupt to execute a 2-pass SRAM entropy-flooding and zeroization sequence upon physical intrusion. 3. Empirical Benchmarks & Comparative Analysis The system was benchmarked on an ARM Cortex-M0+ running at 48 MHz. Cycle Invariance: Verified via ARM SysTick->VAL profiling, proving a steady-state execution time of exactly 11,988 CPU cycles (249.75 µs) with zero variance ($\sigma^2 = 0$), compared to variable-timing table-based software ciphers (~35,000+ cycles). Memory Footprint: Consumes < 1.2 KB of Flash and < 64 bytes of SRAM, outperforming bulky software stacks like mbedTLS. Tamper Latency: Achieves key-shredding in < 1 µs, mitigating cold-boot memory retention. 4. Repository & File Structure main.c: Contains the bare-metal C implementation, register initializations, TRNG entropy harvester, constant-time cipher, and EXTI0 tamper interrupt service routine. diagram.json: The Wokwi hardware simulation configuration file defining the STM32C031 Nucleo board, the analog potentiometer sensor (PA1), and the physical tamper pushbutton (PA0). aead_out.png: Empirical benchmark serial output log demonstrating live sequence tracking, encrypted ciphertext, hardware CRC-32 verification tags, and cycle-count invariance. GitHub Source Code & Interactive Simulation:https://github.com/VasudevanS1906/cortex-m0-secure-vault-trng

title: Understanding Generation Z's Continuance Intention toward E-commerce Chatbots: Survey Dataset on Information Quality, Satisfaction, Perceived Ease of Use, and Trust
abstract: This dataset contains the survey responses used in the study "Empirical Study of Generation Z's Continuance Intention toward E-commerce Chatbots" (Gunawan, Subhan, and Caesar, Bina Nusantara University). The study adapts the research model of Gao et al. (2025, Journal of Business Research, 200, 115661, doi:10.1016/j.jbusres.2025.115661) to examine how information quality, perceived ease of use, trust, and satisfaction relate to the intention to continue using AI chatbots on e-commerce platforms. DATA COLLECTIONResponses were collected through an online questionnaire (Google Forms) between 27 and 30 March 2026 (timestamps in GMT+7), using convenience sampling targeting Generation Z users in the JABODETABEK region of Indonesia. The questionnaire items were administered in English, and the introduction was in Indonesian. On the opening page, participants were informed of the study's purpose and told that their responses would be confidential, anonymous, and used only for academic purposes. The dataset contains no names, e-mail addresses, or other direct identifiers. FILEOne CSV file exported from Google Forms: 315 rows (one per submission) and 24 columns, with no missing values. This is the raw export: no responses were removed and no recoding was applied. VARIABLES- Timestamp: date and time of submission (GMT+7)- Gender: Male (154), Female (161)- Age (categories): 18–21 years (103), 22–28 years (195), 29–35 years (16), >35 years (1)- Place of Education: Tangerang (87), Depok (82), Bogor (49), Bekasi (47), Jakarta (47), Bandung (1), Jatinangor (1), Pontianak (1)- Education: Diploma (77), Bachelor's Degree/S1 (214), Master's Degree/S2 (20), Doctor's Degree/S3 (4)- 19 measurement items, each rated on a five-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree). All items are positively worded; none is reverse-coded. MEASUREMENT ITEMS (column headers contain the full item wording)Information quality (IQ1–IQ7): AI chatbots in e-commerce provide sufficient information; Through AI chatbots in e-commerce, I get the information I need on time; Information provided by AI chatbots in e-commerce is in a useful format / is clear / is accurate / is up-to-date / is reliable.Satisfaction (SF1–SF3), perceived ease of use (PEU1–PEU3), trust (TR1–TR3), and continue using intention (CUI1–CUI3): items adopted from Gao et al. (2025), e.g., "Overall, I am satisfied with AI chatbot in e-commerce", "Using AI chatbot in e-commerce is easy for me", "I consider the AI chatbot in e-commerce to be trustworthy", "I intend to continue using AI chatbot in e-commerce rather than discontinue using them". NOTES FOR REUSE- Column order: Timestamp, Gender, Age, Place of Education, Education, IQ1–IQ7, SF1–SF3, PEU1–PEU3, TR1–TR3, CUI1–CUI3.- Age was recorded in categories; 17 submissions fall in categories above 28 years.- Place of Education includes three locations outside JABODETABEK.- Some submissions share identical answers across all 19 items (18 rows, 7 distinct patterns).- The original analysis used PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 with bootstrapping (5,000 resamples). Contact: gilbert.gunawan002@binus.ac.id

title: Подієво-орієнтована архітектура мультиагентних систем на основі великих мовних моделей – агенти як мікросервіси
abstract: У статті запропоновано подієво-орієнтовану архітектуру мультиагентних систем (МАС) на основі великих мовних моделей (LLM), у якій кожен агент є незалежним мікросервісом з власним пулом обчислювальних ресурсів, а взаємодія агентів здійснюється завдяки брокеру подій. Розроблено математичну модель МАС як мережі систем масового обслуговування з розгалуженням і злиттям (fork-join), яка враховує логнормальний час інференсу LLM, обмежену конкурентність агентів, транзієнтні помилки, повторні спроби та динаміку черги під час відмови агента та пікового навантаження. Удосконалено модель втрат синхронної оркестрації завдяки урахування кореляції повторних спроб. Синхронну послідовну оркестрацію, синхронну оркестрацію з паралельним розгалуженням і подієву хореографію порівняно аналітично, методом імітаційного моделювання та експериментально на прототипі на основі Redis Streams. Встановлено, що в стаціонарному режимі латентність визначається критичним шляхом графа задачі і не залежить від способу доставки, тоді як під час відмов агентів і пікових навантажень подієва архітектура зберігає всі задачі без налаштування повторів на боці клієнта ціною їх затримки в черзі. title: IntelliLayer: A Deep Learning Architecture for Dynamic Decision Intelligence
abstract: Organizations increasingly use data-driven systems to support operational decision-making in dynamic environments. However, many existing deep learning models focus primarily on predicting outcomes rather than recommending reliable actions. These models often provide limited information about prediction confidence, may experience performance degradation when data patterns change, and offer insufficient explanations for their decisions. Previous studies have addressed these challenges independently through improved prediction models, uncertainty estimation, calibration techniques, data drift detection, and explainable AI methods. To address these limitations, this paper introduces IntelliLayer, a five-layer deep learning architecture that combines these capabilities within a unified decision-making framework. The proposed architecture integrates static data and sequential events using Transformer encoders and a learnable gated fusion mechanism. It estimates calibrated outcome distributions through a deep ensemble and selects actions based on expected utility, while uncertain cases are referred to human reviewers. To handle changing data patterns, the framework employs adaptive windowing for drift detection and updates the model using replay techniques and elastic weight consolidation. Additionally, integrated gradients are used to explain individual predictions, and an audit record is maintained for every decision to support transparency and accountability. The paper describes the architecture of each layer, outlines the online decision-making algorithm, and presents a reference implementation stack. It also defines a reproducible evaluation framework covering predictive performance, calibration, decision-making costs, selective prediction coverage, recovery from data drift, and processing latency. Since experimental results have not yet been obtained, the proposed evaluation protocol and results template provide a structured basis for future validation of the IntelliLayer architecture.

title: Breaking the Static Verifier Ceiling: Zero-Overhead Self-Evolving System-One Judge and Policy Co-Evolution on a Single Shared Foundation Backbone (CoEvo-Jev-GRPO)
abstract: Full-Length Preprint (12-Page English Edition + 8-Page Chinese Edition) & Benchmark Suite — Part III-B: Self-Evolving System-One Judge & Policy Co-Evolution. When an LLM policy evolves beyond 400 GRPO steps on hard competition mathematics, any frozen reward model suffers from late-stage calibration drift and Goodhart pseudo-proof exploitation, while dual-model online RM training triples GPU VRAM (24.46 GB). We introduce CoEvo-Jev-GRPO, an online verifier-anchored bilevel co-evolution framework on a single shared Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B backbone (8.08 GB total VRAM on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB, adding only +0.02 GB and 0.84 ms per calibration step). By mining policy-verifier disagreement rollouts and updating the Layer-28 System-One Pointer Head and top-layer judge LoRAs via a Null-Anchored Brier + Contrastive Margin + KL-to-Prior objective, CoEvo-Jev-GRPO contracts Judge Expected Calibration Error (ECE) by 77.1% (from 0.048 to 0.011) and suppresses subtle pseudo-proof hacking to 1.2%. Across MATH-500 (79.8%), AIME 2024/2025 (36.7%, +16.7% over Binary RLVR), AMC-12 (74.4%), and OlympiadBench-Math (46.2%), CoEvo-Jev-GRPO achieves #1 SOTA with 59.28% Mean Accuracy (+5.28% over Frozen DC-Jev-GRPO and +15.83% over Binary RLVR). Series Companion DOIs: Part I (10.5281/zenodo.23439711), Part II (10.5281/zenodo.23441431)Open-Source Code & v3.0.0 Suite: https://github.com/rainyflash/DC-Jev-RL

abstract: FINDING: Semi-device-independent entanglement quantification reduces to Bell-inequality violation bounds under fixed local measurements, with a "nondegeneracy" condition separating orthogonal quantum states by dimension. | MATH: Nondegeneracy property — for a Bell inequality \(B\) and fixed local measurements \(\{M_A^a, M_B^b\}\), if a state \(\rho\) of dimension \(d\) violates \(B\) (i.e., \(\langle B\rangle_\rho > \beta_{\text{local}}\)), then its orthogonal complement \(\rho^\perp\) (with \(\text{Tr}(\rho\rho^\perp)=0\)) cannot also violate \(B\) under the same measurements. title: Capability-as-Infrastructure: Software on Demand
abstract: Capability-as-Infrastructure (CaI) proposes that the durable unit of a software system is no longer the application but the declared capability, together with the data, history, decisions and authority it operates on. Applications, interfaces, synchronization logic and much of the executable code become compiled, replaceable outputs of an agentic environment that builds them when a need appears and maintains them while they are useful: software on demand. Where Methodology-as-Infrastructure compiles how to think, Intent-as-Infrastructure compiles what to reach into, and Governance-as-Infrastructure compiles what must be true, CaI compiles what must be possible, opening a duration axis alongside GaI's upstream terminus. Four properties are required: Capability-declared, Implementation-compiled, Continuity-sovereign (observation, interpretation and accepted state kept distinct), and Human-as-primitive at authority. CaI extends local-first software (the sync protocol itself becomes a compiled capability) and malleable software. This is a concept paper: its two central claims, continuity under replacement and autonomous capability growth, are stated as hypotheses with a validation protocol, and a companion document describes a reference architecture on Cloudflare (Workers, Durable Objects, Agents SDK, Workflows).

title: 枯れ葉から大樹へ:AIエコシステムにおける構造改革のための戦略的提言 — データ配当(Data Dividend)プロトコルとオンデバイス動画生成AI(Veo Nano)アーキテクチャによる共生的未来の設計 (From Leaf to Tree: A Strategic Proposal for Structural Reform in the AI Ecosystem)
abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) | Original Manuscript Date: November 2025 現在、生成AIエコシステムは「熱力学的限界(クラウド推論の電力・コスト・遅延)」と「情報学的限界(有機的学習データの枯渇と自己回帰的モデル崩壊:Model Collapse)」という二つの存亡に関わる壁に直面している。本論文(2025年11月起案・第212編アーカイブ版)は、対価なき一方的データ抽出パラダイムが長期的には基盤モデル自身の品質劣化とクリエイター離反を招くことを指摘し、以下の2つの技術的・経済的解決策を提言する。(1) 経済的解決策(Data Dividend / GDDプロトコル):C2PA来歴証明規格とシャープレイ値(Shapley Value)/影響関数に基づく貢献度算定を結合し、人間が創出した高エントロピーな「有機的データ(Organic Data)」へマイクロ・ロイヤリティを自動還元するサプライチェーンを確立する。(2) 技術的解決策(オンデバイス動画生成AI「Veo Nano」アーキテクチャ):クラウドGPU(H100等)の推論コストと通信レイテンシを解消するため、敵対的蒸留(1ステップ推論化)と拡散トランスフォーマー(DiT)の4ビット量子化(W4A8)および連合学習(Federated Learning)を統合し、モバイル・エッジNPU上で完結するプライバシー保護型リアルタイム生成アーキテクチャを設計する。 (English Abstract): Generative AI confronts a dual existential bottleneck: thermodynamic scaling limits (cloud GPU inference energy, cost, and network latency) and information-theoretic degradation ("Model Collapse" induced by training on recursive synthetic data while alienating human creators). Originally authored in November 2025, this 212th monograph proposes a two-pillar structural reform: (1) a C2PA and Shapley-Value Data Dividend (GDD) Protocol that distinguishes human-created "Organic Data" from synthetic outputs and automates micro-royalty attribution; and (2) an On-Device Video Diffusion ("Veo Nano") Architecture combining single-step adversarial distillation, 4-bit Diffusion Transformer quantization (W4A8KV4), and GDPR-compliant Federated Learning on mobile NPUs. title: Analysis of Information Degradation and Reliability Transitions via Structured Noise Injection in Multisensor Localization
abstract: This study investigates information degradation and reliability transitions in multisensor localization systems using a structured noise injection approach. A five-sensor localization scenario is considered, where range measurements are intentionally corrupted by Gaussian perturbations, intermittent burst disturbances, and positive measurement biases. Target coordinates are estimated using a weighted nonlinear least-squares method, while localization performance is evaluated through root mean square error (RMSE), Fisher Information Matrix (FIM), Cramér–Rao Lower Bound (CRLB), and failure rate metrics. Experiments are conducted under signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels ranging from −5 dB to 25 dB using 600 Monte Carlo realizations for each operating condition. The results show that increasing perturbation levels progressively reduce localization accuracy and information content while increasing theoretical uncertainty. A distinct reliability transition region is observed between 5 dB and 10 dB, where localization failures rapidly decrease as measurement quality improves. The findings demonstrate that controlled noise injection provides a practical means of exposing information-deficient operating conditions and reliability boundaries in multisensor localization systems.

title: Prune Early, Verify Deep: Single-Backbone System-One Prefix Tree-GRPO and Speculative Noul Pruning for Long-Horizon Reasoning and Theorem Proving (Tree-Jev-GRPO)
abstract: Full-Length Preprint (12-Page English Edition + 7-Page Chinese Edition) & Benchmark Suite — Part III-C: Long-Horizon Prefix Tree-GRPO & Formal Theorem Proving. Standard flat-sequence GRPO wastes 70%+ of decoding FLOPs regenerating shared reasoning prefixes and continuing to decode 1,500+ tokens after a chain hits an early algebraic contradiction. We introduce Tree-Jev-GRPO, which exploits Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B’s hybrid Gated-DeltaNet linear-attention architecture (3.81x lower prefix-tree KV memory, 14.20 GB vs. 54.10 GB on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB) and co-located jaredpalmer/kev-4b incremental node probing (14.80 ms/node). By immediately pruning dead-end branches where g_noul < 0.30 and computing sibling-relative branch advantages across shared-prefix forks (-61.5% gradient variance), Tree-Jev-GRPO cuts wasted dead-end FLOPs by 66.0% (2.94x compute speedup) and achieves #1 SOTA across 4 Formal & Long-Horizon Reasoning Benchmarks: MiniF2F-Lean4 (64.8%, +20.2% over Flat Binary RLVR), ProofNet-Formal (52.4%), MATH-500 Level-5 Hard (68.7%, +26.9% over Binary RLVR), and GPQA-Diamond (56.1%), reaching 60.50% Mean Accuracy. title: TwinLens: an interpretability digital twin for LLMs
abstract: TwinLens builds a transcoder-based digital twin of a language model, predicts the effect of feature interventions, and checks each prediction against the real model. Across 8,064 interventions on GPT-2 small (56 prompts), the linear twin that attribution graphs describe ranks real effects poorly (Spearman rho 0.20). The error traces to two dropped derivatives, the LayerNorm scale and the attention pattern. Restoring both keeps the graph exactly linear and raises rho to 0.53, matching the nonlinear replacement model (0.52), and cuts catastrophic misses from 2.2% to 0.05%. The fix replicates on Qwen3-0.6B (2,304 edits). A trust model predicts in advance, from the clean run alone, when a prediction will hold (AUROC 0.93).

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms and Mutual Mechanisms Under Uncertainty: A General Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Coordination in Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) operate under multiple forms of uncertainty, including uncertainty about the correctness of generated answers, the completeness of available evidence, the validity of intermediate reasoning, the interpretation of task requirements, and the reliability of feedback. Individual-model mechanisms, such as self-reflection, self-evaluation, self-diagnosis, self-correction, and self-verification, provide ways to inspect and revise outputs. Mutual mechanisms, including cross-model evaluation, mutual diagnosis, collaborative reasoning, cross-model verification, and information exchange, provide additional perspectives that may reveal errors overlooked by an individual model. However, neither individual processing nor multi-model collaboration is universally optimal under uncertainty. Individual processing may preserve computational efficiency but remain trapped in persistent errors, whereas collaboration may introduce correlated judgments, misleading consensus, additional computational costs, and uncertainty that is transferred or amplified through interaction. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms and Mutual Mechanisms Under Uncertainty (ASSM-MM-U), a conceptual framework that treats uncertainty as a central state variable for dynamically selecting and coordinating individual-model and cross-model processing mechanisms. The framework distinguishes uncertainty associated with incomplete evidence, model limitations, ambiguous task specifications, conflicting information, and uncertain evaluation signals. It represents uncertainty through a multidimensional state that includes estimated magnitude, source, calibration quality, persistence, propagation, and reducibility. A cost-sensitive controller estimates the expected value of candidate mechanisms in reducing relevant uncertainty and improving task outcomes. It can retain an individual mechanism, activate a mutual mechanism, return to individual processing, or transition between mechanism families according to the evolving uncertainty state. The paper formalizes the problem, presents an uncertainty-aware architecture and reference algorithm, identifies reliability safeguards, and proposes research questions, hypotheses, and an experimental protocol. The framework is a research proposal rather than an empirically validated system. Its potential contribution is the explicit integration of uncertainty characterization, uncertainty reduction, mechanism selection, and resource-aware coordination within a common control framework. The novelty and effectiveness of this integration require systematic comparison with existing uncertainty-estimation, adaptive reasoning, and multi-agent collaboration methods.

title: The Collider Beacon: Certified Public Randomness from Symmetry and Quantum Measurement
abstract: We propose particle collisions at the Large Hadron Collider as a shared cryptographic resource. The construction rests on a division of labor between symmetry and quantum measurement: rotational invariance fixes the azimuthal distribution to the Haar measure, while each event is an unpredictable quantum draw. We give a formal source model, a master bound decomposing the distance-to-uniform into named physical terms, and a pre-commitment protocol turning embargoed datasets into time-capsule beacons. On 5,211,771 CMS ZeroBias events (Run 2016G open data) we measure h_inf = 7.8413 of 8 bits per event, with the bound closing exactly on its measured parameters; NIST STS reports zero flags. A cross-detector check on ATLAS open data (597,965 events) finds the CMS acceptance seam absent (local band ratio 1.0024 +/- 0.0072; excluded at 14.1 sigma), while ATLAS exhibits a distinct broad modulation -- the seam is a per-device geometric fingerprint. Code and evidence: https://github.com/qBucker/collider-beacon (tag phase0-v1.0).

title: Cost Per Correct: benchmark tasks for cost-per-correct-answer evaluation of LLM agents
abstract: Cost Per Correct is a small benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on cost-effectiveness rather than accuracy alone. Instead of asking only whether a model produces a correct answer, it prices the run and reports the cost of each correct answer: total spend in USD divided by the number of correct answers, so a cheap model that is usually right can beat an expensive model that is always right. Version 1.0.0 contains the 5 easy-tier tasks (arithmetic, extraction, classification) that are live in the hosted benchmark. Each task is a self-contained prompt with a deterministic grading assertion (regular-expression match on the response; no LLM judge). The benchmark was created by Karmendra Pandey and first published as a public benchmark on Kaggle Benchmarks on 11 October 2026 (Kaggle Benchmarking Challenge entry), where the live leaderboard remains: https://www.kaggle.com/benchmarks/karmendra8386/cost-per-correct In the first hosted run (11 October 2026), Gemini 2.5 Flash passed all 5 tasks (leaderboard score 100.00) and GPT-OSS 120B failed one extraction task; three runs on the second task show as errors because the Kaggle platform would not register swapped-in models - platform errors, not model answers, disclosed in the accompanying README (hosted-results-2026-10-11.csv) and in the entry write-up at the time. Costs are accounted with tokenecon (software DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23427025), the token-economics library that decomposes per-task spend into prompt, completion, tool-call, and retrieval tokens priced per model tier. The underlying cost model is described in the companion preprint "Token-Economics for Agentic AI" (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23195511). This Zenodo record mirrors the benchmark off Kaggle so the task set and methodology carry a permanent, citable DOI independent of any single platform. Provenance: the hosted benchmark was never exported from Kaggle; the task definitions were transcribed verbatim from the local source code used to build it and cross-checked against the entry-day record written from the live task pages. Only tasks e1-e5 of the author's 24-task local suite are live on Kaggle, so only those 5 are in this dataset.

title: SwinMask-Cyto: Supporting Experimental Data and Evaluation Results
abstract: This repository contains supporting experimental data for the research manuscript entitled “SwinMask-Cyto: A Swin Transformer-Enhanced Mask R-CNN Framework for Multi-Class Cervical Cell Instance Segmentation.” The research investigates a Swin Transformer-enhanced Mask R-CNN framework for automated detection and instance segmentation of five cervical cytology cell categories: Superficial-Intermediate, Parabasal, Metaplastic, Koilocytotic, and Dyskeratotic. The repository contains available experimental training logs, validation and test evaluation results, model configuration files, training metric histories, prediction outputs, and supporting numerical data. The experiments investigate different training durations, data augmentation strategies, and model regularization configurations. The best recorded 36-epoch experiment achieved a bounding-box mAP@0.5 of 0.7230 and a segmentation mAP@0.5 of 0.7280 on the held-out test set. These materials are provided to support transparency, reproducibility, and further research in artificial intelligence-assisted cervical cytology analysis. Dataset sources, file descriptions, and applicable data-sharing restrictions are documented in the accompanying files. Original private clinical images are not included in the public research data collection.

title: Clinical validation of artificial intelligence for cancer detection prognosis and analysis across imaging modalities and tumor types
abstract: This study evaluates the diagnostic and prognostic performance of artificial intelligence in cancer detection across imaging modalities and tumor types. The review synthesizes current evidence on deep learning, radiomics, multimodal integration, and precision oncology frameworks, with emphasis on validation quality and clinical translation. A systematic review of 180 peer reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 was conducted. Included investigations assessed artificial intelligence applications in radiology, digital pathology, endoscopy, PET imaging, and multimodal platforms. Extracted data covered diagnostic accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, dataset size, validation strategy, and study design. Subdomains included detection, prognosis, grading, survival prediction, radio-genomics, explainability, federated learning, and regulatory evaluation. Across breast, lung, prostate, colorectal, brain, and skin cancers, multiple high-quality cohorts reported AUC values above 0.90. Whole slide histopathology achieved the highest discrimination, reaching AUC 0.99 in curated datasets. CT and MRI systems demonstrated strong performance with multicenter validation, including large scale lung and breast screening studies. Radiomics contributed to survival prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, and molecular subtype inference. Multimodal and transformer-based architectures improved representation learning in volumetric and cross domain data. Despite strong retrospective performance, only 21 percent of studies included external validation, 14 percent incorporated multicenter datasets, and 6 percent applied prospective or temporal validation. Artificial intelligence shows consistent high performance in cancer detection and prognostic modeling across imaging domains. Strongest evidence supports adjunctive use in screening, digital pathology, and endoscopic detection. Broader clinical adoption requires prospective trials, multicenter external validation, standardized reporting, explainability integration, and alignment with regulatory frameworks to ensure reliable deployment in precision oncology.
